# candy-code & candy-code-web vs Claude Code, OpenCode and OpenClaw

_A feature-by-feature comparison of candy-code and candy-code-web against Claude Code 2.1.311, OpenCode 1.19.4 and 2.1.4, and OpenClaw 2026.10.7, describing each product as it stands on 2026-10-26. Appendix A holds the per-cell detail and evidence._

| Product | Version compared | How it was examined |
|---|---|---|
| **candy-code** (PHP TUI agent) | monorepo `master`, 2026-10-26 | Code audits traced from `bin/candy-code` with live runs in tmux and headless, then a static re-audit of `master` on 2026-10-26 in three passes covering all 25 categories |
| **candy-code-web** (Vue 3 browser UI for `candy-code serve`) | 0.1.0 (prebuilt `dist/` committed), monorepo `master`, 2026-10-26 | Code audit, typecheck, lint, unit tests and live probes of a throwaway server (curl, WebSocket, headless Chromium), then the same static re-audit of `master` on 2026-10-26 |
| **Claude Code** | 2.1.311 (installed here; npm `latest` 2.1.311, `stable` 2.1.308) | All 228 official doc pages, the changelog through 2.1.311, `--help` for every subcommand, and a read-only look at `~/.claude` |
| **OpenCode** | **1.19.4** (latest v1; 1.18.35 is installed here) and **2.1.4** (latest v2; not installed here) | Source at 1.18.35, 1.19.4, 2.0.31 and 2.1.4, shipped docs and changelogs, CLI help, local configs and installed plugins. 1.18.35 → 1.19.4 changes only updates, session sharing, reasoning variants and the bundled Bun |
| **OpenClaw** | 2026.10.7 (npm latest; installed baseline 2026.9.8) | The 2026.10.7 npm package's ~1,300 doc pages and `dist/` source (diffed against the installed 2026.9.8), CLI help, the `clawhub` CLI, and GitHub changelogs to 2026.10.7 |

| 🟡 | Partial or limited (the cell says what's missing) |
| 🔌 | Only via a named plugin or extension |
| 🧪 | Code exists but is dormant, i.e. not reachable from the live app (candy-code and candy-code-web columns only) |
| ❌ | Absent |

> **Read the scoreboard with one caveat.** The candy-code and candy-code-web columns come from *adversarial code audits*: a feature with a real bug or an unreachable path was marked 🟡 or 🧪. The competitor columns come from each product's docs, source and CLI help, and their bugs were only counted when the researchers happened to find one (e.g. OpenCode's never-fired `permission.ask` hook). Raw ✅ counts therefore flatter the competitors relative to candy-code. Read the cells, not just the totals.

## 1. Bottom line

**candy-code's engine is genuinely competitive.**
- **Where it matches the best of the three:**
  - native memory with hybrid recall and consolidation (on a par with OpenClaw, ahead of Claude Code and OpenCode);
  - DNS-pinned SSRF protection (on a par with OpenClaw);
  - live sub-agent control (it edges out Claude Code with pause, broadcast and a shared batch board);
  - discoverability: a startup summary (version, model, mode, loaded instruction files, counts, a tip), `/context` naming the instruction files it read, and full `/skills`, `/agents` and `/hooks` listings.
- **Where it is ahead:**
  - prompt-injection fencing of instruction files;
  - model-callable context-pruning tools;
  - git-versioned memory history;
  - a settings view that shows where each value comes from.
- It **trails on two fronts:**
  - **Breadth.** Providers (no native subscription OAuth, Azure or OpenRouter type, or Responses API), MCP (no elicitation, sampling, roots or server mode), hooks (12 events, shell commands only), no plugin marketplace, no VS Code extension, native JetBrains plugin, desktop, mobile or chat surfaces (editors connect only through ACP), and scheduling only through the user's `/loop` and `/schedules` (no model-callable tool).
  - **TUI rough edges.** vim mode has normal/visual motions and the visual `d`/`y`/`x` operators but no counts, text objects, `cw` or named registers; the TUI paints no live shell output; there is no screen-reader mode; `statusLine` gets no session JSON.

**candy-code-web is a strong multi-session cockpit**, with a careful sign-in design and lossless reconnect, but it **exposes only part of the engine**:
- 8 of the 69 protocol methods are never requested from the browser: `files.read`, `memory.log`, `memory.undo`, `session.share`, `session.unshare`, `workflow.status`, `workspace.close`, and the Admin-scope `server.shutdown` (which arrives as a notification and is handled).
- 16 built-ins have no host body and are refused `ui_only` over the wire: `/new`, `/sessions`, `/effort`, `/exit`, `/theme`, `/settings`, `/keys`, `/help`, `/compress`, `/newrule`, `/pane`, `/layout`, `/editor`, `/budget`, `/review` and `/security-review` (`/theme`, `/settings`, `/sessions` and `/new` have web-native equivalents). The other 41 run on the server, `/model`, `/compact`, `/init`, `/goal`, `/grind`, `/btw`, `/hooks` and `/skills` among them.
- The Context panel (`context.sources`) lists loaded instruction files (path, size, tier), refused files, memory notes, skills (name and tier) and project MCP servers (configured status, no liveness), with a project-trust prompt; hooks show only through the server-run `/hooks` text table. `@mcp:` mentions, MCP prompt commands, `/mcp login` and `/skill-name` do not work in served sessions, and runtime notices (memory recall, model fallback) never reach the browser because serve does not drain the notice sink. Served sessions also run no turn-end auto-memory or dream pass, and refuse `/btw` while a turn runs.
- Background sessions inherit the server's permission mode and route their asks to the approvals drawer; a `/loop` typed in the browser registers but never fires (the served host has no ephemeral-schedule pump).

| | Where candy-code **leads** | Where it is **at parity** | Where it **trails** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context & memory | Instruction-file fencing/escaping with provenance preambles (unique; Claude Code scrubs only MEMORY.md); named budget overflow; native `Prune`/`Compress`/`Recall` tools (OpenCode needs a plugin: DCP on 1.x, magic-context on either major; Claude Code and OpenClaw have none); git-versioned memory with `/memory log`/`restore` (OpenClaw only git-inits its workspace); repo-shareable memory; summaries pre-fetched ahead of need (TUI and served sessions) | Hybrid memory recall + consolidation + pre-compaction flush (as OpenClaw); compaction with structured state; `/context` breakdown; `/btw`; checkpoints/rewind | No managed-policy instructions, system-prompt append or output styles (Claude Code has all three); no per-sub-agent memory; no prompt-cache warming; served sessions skip turn-end auto-memory and the dream pass |
| Agents | Finest live run control: **pause**, **broadcast** and a shared per-batch board (BoardPost/BoardRead), on top of type-into-child, cancel, background, 7-day resume and worktree isolation (which Claude Code also has) | Parallel + nested + background sub-agents and teams (as Claude Code and OpenClaw) | No `@agent` mention; no agent wizard |
| Extensibility | Reads foreign **agents** live (`.claude/agents`, `.opencode/agents`; no competitor does) as well as foreign skills (`.claude`, `.agents`, `.opencode`) and foreign commands (`.claude/commands`, `.opencode/command(s)`); MCP server fingerprint pinning | Skill gating by bins/env/os (shared only with OpenClaw); fail-closed shell hooks by default that parse Claude Code's JSON verdict envelope and deliver the Claude-shaped JSON payload on stdin like Claude Code does; custom commands with `$ARGUMENTS`/`` !`cmd` ``/`@file` | no plugin registry or marketplace (bundles import Claude-format plugins); no MCP elicitation, sampling, roots or server mode, and MCP resources and prompts are TUI-only; 12 hook events vs Claude Code's 33, and a Claude settings file with non-`command` hook types or newer entry keys refuses the launch; no forked or tool-restricted skills |
| Tools & safety | Built-in apply-patch for every model and LSP diagnostics fed back after edits (Claude Code: no apply-patch, LSP feedback via plugin; OpenClaw: apply-patch for every model but no plan mode or LSP feedback; OpenCode 1.x: LSP feedback, apply-patch for GPT models only); scripted PTY driver built in (OpenClaw's `exec pty` + `process send-keys` is comparable; OpenCode 1.x needs the opencode-pty plugin and 2.1.4 has only an experimental, write-only `write_terminal`; Claude Code has none); shell-aware rule engine; SSRF guard (DNS-pinned, full special-range blocklist) far beyond Claude Code's and OpenCode's | Plan mode, ask-user, todo; six-stage edit matcher requiring a unique match per stage (Claude Code is exact-only; OpenCode 1.x and OpenClaw also match fuzzily); content-hash stale-file refusal (Claude Code enforces read-before-edit instead; OpenCode and OpenClaw have neither); policy self-grant floor (only Claude Code matches); SSRF on a par with OpenClaw; opt-in bubblewrap sandbox for Bash and PtyRun that fails closed by default (Claude Code's sandbox is broader, with Seatbelt and a network allowlist, but fails closed only with `failIfUnavailable`) | Auto mode is a regex classifier (with an opt-in LLM reviewer fed flagged calls and every unflagged non-read-only shell call), where Claude Code runs a model-based classifier (server-side review, else a client-side model); auto-format and LSP auto-detect are opt-in, with no bundled formatter table and no LSP auto-install; no notebook, browser-control or code-mode tool; WebFetch returns raw HTML; Read answers PDFs with a `pdftotext` hint and `@`-mentioned PDFs ride document blocks only on Anthropic and Vertex-Claude; the TUI paints no live shell output |
| Providers | Deepest self-hosted (SGLang) support; explicit no-total-timeout engineering; mid-stream resume of a dropped stream | Bedrock, Vertex, a Gemini API-key provider, OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Claude Code has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint; OpenClaw's Bedrock is a plugin); fallback models (as Claude Code and OpenClaw) | No native subscription OAuth (`candy-code login` hands off to `claude auth login` / `codex login` or stores an API key); no Azure or OpenRouter type, no OpenAI Responses API, no OS keychain |
| Sessions & automation | Typed JSON error document on every CLI failure with test-pinned exit codes (OpenClaw's `agent exec` is similar) | Single-writer session locking, background daemons, `/goal` judge loop (as Claude Code and OpenClaw; OpenCode has no lock and `/goal` only via opencode-goal-plugin, which runs on both majors); resume/continue/branch/fork/export | webhook triggers are serve-only (no outbound); share links need a running `serve` (no hosted endpoint); no session import; `/loop` never fires in a served session |
| UX | Generated, drift-tested keyboard reference; contrast-aware themes (unique); settings view with source + apply mode; dockable panes; inline images with kitty/iTerm2/sixel/chafa/half-block fallbacks (OpenClaw: Kitty/iTerm2/Ghostty thumbnails only) | Status bar, permission modal depth with diff preview, steering (Enter/Tab/Esc), fuzzy `@` file popup, Ctrl+G history search, rebindable keymap with `/keys reload` | the startup summary is four text rows (no logo, effort, account or announcements); no screen-reader mode; vim lacks counts, text objects, `cw` and registers; `statusLine` gets no session JSON |
| Surfaces | Self-hostable browser cockpit (multi-session tabs + 3×3 grid, server-wide approvals) with gap-free seq-cursor reconnect in candy-code-web | One engine behind TUI, web, `attach` and ACP clients (as OpenCode's server and OpenClaw's Gateway); lossless reconnect in both clients (OpenClaw and OpenCode 2.x replay too; `candy-code attach` redials with backoff and resumes from its cursor); ACP for Zed/JetBrains/Neovim | No VS Code extension or native JetBrains plugin (Claude Code has both; OpenCode has the VS Code extension); no desktop, mobile, chat channels or cloud execution; Linux-first, no Windows; Composer, release PHAR (`self-update`) or the serve Docker image only (no npm, brew or curl installer) |

## 3. Full feature matrix

The matrix has **409 rows**, each with **6 product columns**: the 356-row taxonomy plus 53 🆕 rows for features found during research.
- **Cells:** each holds a status code and a summary of at most 130 characters. The full *how / when / where shown* detail and the evidence (file:line, doc URL) for every cell is in [Appendix A](#appendix-a--per-feature-detail-how-when-where-evidence).
- **Category rows:** bold rows start each of the 25 categories.

> **Coverage.** candy-code and candy-code-web are rated from their source on monorepo `master` (2026-10-26); each competitor is rated at the version in its column header. In the OpenCode 2.1.4 column, `Δ` marks a cell that differs from the OpenCode 1.19.4 cell; an unmarked cell describes the same behaviour. 🆕 rows are rated like any other row but are not counted in the §2 scoreboard, and a `· Not assessed` cell in a 🆕 row means that product's research did not cover the feature.

## 4. How and when each tool surfaces context, to the model and to the user

The OpenCode cells in this section describe the 1.x line (1.19.4; this host runs 1.18.35, which still advertises session sharing although the share host is gone); §5.1 lists what 2.1.4 changes. The big table says *whether* a product has a feature. This section covers the question that matters most day to day: **what the model is actually given, at what moment, and what the human can see of it.** "Web" means what a browser user of candy-code-web can see; the engine behind it is the same as the TUI's.

### 4.1 Instruction files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / rules)

| | candy-code (TUI) | candy-code-web | Claude Code 2.1.311 | OpenCode 1.19.4 | OpenClaw 2026.10.7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Files read** | `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.clinerules` at every level; personal `~/.candy-code/AGENTS.md`; user-tier `instructions` globs; own rules tier (`~/.candy-code/rules`, `rulebooks/`, `<root>/.candy-code/rules`, `RULES.md`); foreign tiers `CLAUDE.local.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (personal stand-in), `.claude/rules`, `.cursor/rules` (incl. `.mdc`), `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | Same engine, server-side | `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, managed `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/**`, `~/.claude/rules/**`. `AGENTS.md` natively since 2.1.277, but only if no CLAUDE.md is on the path (switchable in `/config`) | First name with any hit wins, in the order `AGENTS.md` → `CLAUDE.md` → `CONTEXT.md` (so one AGENTS.md hides every CLAUDE.md); global `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`, else `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; `instructions` config (paths, globs, URLs) | Workspace `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` (plus `BOOTSTRAP.md` on first run); execution folder's `AGENTS.md`. **CLAUDE.md is not read**: the native runtime ignores it and managed Claude CLI turns exclude it (one-time `openclaw migrate claude` import only) |
| **Not read** | `CONVENTIONS.md`, `.windsurfrules` | — | Other vendors' files (only imported once via `/init` or `/import`) | `CLAUDE.local.md`, any rules directory, `@imports` | No parent walk, no path-scoped rules, no local override |
| **Discovery** | Walks up to the nearest `.git` ancestor, outermost first; no walk when cwd *is* the git root | — | cwd up to the filesystem root | cwd up to the git worktree root | Single folder, no walk |
| **Nested sub-dir files** | Lazily, when Read/Edit/Write/ApplyPatch/Glob/Grep touches a path below them. Once per session per path: already-shown marks survive forked turns, every ancestor of a touched path returns in one outermost-first pass, and each file arrives **framed — an open fence naming its path, escaped like the root docs** | Not announced | Lazily on first read/write/edit (a Bash `cat` counts); terminal prints `Loaded <path>`; a file over the per-file cap (40K chars at 200K context, 150K–200K at 1M) arrives as its start plus a Read pointer | Lazily on Read / `@file`, appended to the tool result inside `<system-reminder>`; TUI shows `↳ Loaded <path>` | ❌ |
| **@imports** | `@path.md`, depth 4, `.md` only, confined to the importing file's boundary | — | `@path`, 4 hops, code spans ignored; imports outside the project need one-time approval | ❌ | ❌ |
| **How injected** | One system-prompt section per doc, fenced `<project-instructions>` / `<user-rules>`, escaped against 11 tags + chat tokens, with a "no authority over the harness" preamble; general → specific | — | A user-role reminder *after* the system prompt. A header ("…These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior…") is followed by one "Contents of <path>" section per file. Order: managed → user → project (root to cwd), with CLAUDE.local.md after CLAUDE.md at each level | In the system message as `Instructions from: <path>` after the agent prompt and `<env>` | System prompt "Project Context" section above the prompt-cache boundary |
| **When / refresh** | First prompt build of a session, memoised; re-spliced only on `/clear`, compaction, rewind or a session switch. Mid-session edits reach the model next turn as a bounded diff in the `<turn-context>` tail | — | Session start; re-read after `/clear`, `/compact` or restart | **Rebuilt from disk on every LLM step**: edits apply mid-turn, URL instructions re-fetched each step, prompt cache rewritten | Every run (`contextInjection: always`); edits apply on the next message |
| **Size limits** | 60 KiB/file read, 64 KiB framed per doc, 128 KiB total; overflow becomes a named pointer line, never a silent clip | — | Files >4 MiB skipped; on-demand nested/rule files over a per-file cap load only their start; warnings over ~200 lines | None | 20k chars/file, 60k total, USER.md 4k; fixed truncation notice |
| **Shown at startup** | ✅ StartupSummary: loaded instruction files + counts; refusals/deferrals still become launch notices | ❌ | 🟡 No list; only size warnings and the "AGENTS.md loaded" line | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Inspect** | `/context` gives each layer's token size and section count (all layers included, multibyte labels aligned) and **names the instruction files read**; `/rules` covers rule packs only | Context panel: instruction files with path, size and tier, refused files under "Not read", memory, skills, MCP; `/context` text too | `/context` lists memory files with token costs; `/memory` lists every location; `InstructionsLoaded` hook | ❌ (only the `↳ Loaded` lines) | `/context list/detail/map` (per-file raw vs injected, truncation), Control UI Agents → Files |
| **Edit from UI** | ❌ (`/memory open` edits memory notes, not instruction files; `/newrule` has the agent draft a rule file) | ❌ (the Memory panel edits notes only) | `/memory` opens files in `$EDITOR` | ❌ | Control UI file editor |
| **Generate** | `/init` (TUI and served) | ✅ typed `/init` runs on the host | `/init` (plus a multi-phase variant) | `/init` | 🟡 first-run BOOTSTRAP ritual, no repo analysis |
| **Trust gate** | ❌ (mitigated by fencing/escaping) | ❌ | 🟡 Folder trust dialog, but CLAUDE.md itself isn't trust-gated | ❌ | ❌ |

**Take-aways.**
- candy-code has the *safest* instruction pipeline of the four: fenced, escaped, with provenance preambles and named budget overflow.
- Its nested path is fenced and fork-safe, and it is also the most *visible*: the startup summary and `/context` name the loaded files, the web Context panel lists them, and `instructionsExclude` silences a file with a recorded refusal. What it lacks is an in-app editor for instruction files and a trust gate.
- Claude Code and OpenClaw also name the files on demand (`/memory`, `/context list`), and both can open them for editing, which candy-code cannot.

### 4.2 Memory

| | candy-code | candy-code-web | Claude Code | OpenCode | OpenClaw |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Native?** | ✅ | ✅ (panel) | ✅ (auto memory) | ❌ plugins only (`opencode-agent-memory` on this host; supermemory, honcho, oc-mnemoria, magic-context) | ✅ |
| **Store** | `~/.candy-code/memory/<scope>/*.md` (a private **git repo**: `/memory log`, `/memory restore`) + repo-local `<repo>/.candy-code/memory/project/` (shareable) | — | `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`: `MEMORY.md` index + typed topic files | Plugin-defined | Workspace Markdown (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`) + SQLite FTS5/vector index |
| **Reaches the model** | System prompt: `<project-memory>` **index** (one line per note, 40 entries / 4 KB, frozen per session). **Per turn**: `<memory-recall>`, up to 3 notes ranked BM25 + optional embeddings + recency + MMR, in the user-role tail row (cache-friendly) | — | First 200 lines / 25 KB of `MEMORY.md` in the session-start reminder; topic files read on demand; side-model "recall" step | Plugin injects blocks via `system.transform` | `MEMORY.md` + `USER.md` every run (private sessions only); trigger-phrase recall (no model call) adds up to 3 entries; Active Memory sub-agent for "about the past" turns; `memory_search` / `memory_get` |
| **Who writes, when** | `Memory` tool (no prompt, even in plan mode); auto-memory at turn end (5-min throttle) and a **dream pass** every 2 h over the compaction journal, both from TUI sessions only; pre-compaction flush (prints a saved-rows notice row) | Panel add/edit/delete; served sessions run no auto-memory or dream pass | Claude, during the session (typed `user/feedback/project/reference`); hard index-size hygiene | Plugin | Agent via write/edit; silent pre-compaction flush; default-on **dreaming** (gated promotion, taint gate, `DREAMS.md` diary); optional session-memory hook; imports |
| **User told?** | ✅ Notices for auto/dream writes and the flush (names its saved rows) plus a per-turn "Recalled N notes" row (count only; TUI only, since serve never drains the notice sink) | Tool card only | ✅ "Saved N memories" / "Recalled N memories" with clickable files | Tool rows | 🟡 Mostly silent unless `/verbose` or `/trace` |
| **User UI** | `/memory list/add/search/edit/delete/clear/import/log/restore` (text) + `/memory open <id>` in `$EDITOR` | ✅ Best UI (scope tabs, ranked search, inline edit) over both stores — HOME and repo/project notes list, search, edit and delete alike, and panel writes commit to memory history | `/memory` (toggle, open folder) | ❌ | Control UI Memory (Dreams diary, Wiki), `openclaw memory` CLI |

**Take-aways.**
- candy-code and OpenClaw have the richest memory systems: hybrid recall, consolidation and a pre-compaction flush. OpenClaw's imports reach the prompt; candy-code's land in a non-prompt scope.
- candy-code adds git-versioned history with `/memory log` / `restore`. OpenClaw only git-initializes its workspace (manual commits, no log or undo); Claude Code and OpenCode have none.
- Claude Code's memory is simpler but the most *transparent*: its saved/recalled rows link the files. candy-code's TUI also reports saves and a recall count, but the web shows neither.
- User and model notes in the repo store carry their own author labels. A note added mid-session joins the `<project-memory>` index at the next refresh point (`/clear`, compaction, rewind) or in the next session.

| **Model sees** | `<available-skills>` fenced listing in the system prompt **every turn** with a "MUST load the matching skill" mandate (whole listing bounded by `skills.listingMaxBytes`, ranked truncation) | — | System-reminder listing, budgeted to 1% of context (least-used lose descriptions first) | XML list in the system prompt + pointer in the `skill` tool | `<available_skills>` (name, description, path), budgeted; omitted skills found via `skills_search` |

| **User invokes** | `/skill-name args` or a `$name` mention (one turn, Tab completes); the Ctrl+S picker enables a skill's prompt for the following turns | 🟡 `$name` resolves server-side; `/skill-name` is sent as prose | `/skill-name args` | Every skill is also a `/command` | `/skill <name>`, `/name`, `$name` |
| **User sees list** | ✅ `/skills` lists the installed, invocable table (tiers, disabled, shadowed); dream-pass drafts sit behind `/skills proposed` | ✅ Context panel (name, tier, disabled) + server-run `/skills` table | `/skills` (filter, sort by token cost, visibility toggles) | `/skills` searchable dialog | Control UI Plugins → Skills, `$` picker, `skills list/check` |

| **Registry** | 🟡 none; `bundles install <git-url/path>` installs Claude-format plugin bundles | ❌ | Plugin marketplaces (official catalog: 315 entries) + claude.ai sync | `skills.urls` | ClawHub (security-scanned) |

**Take-away.** candy-code reads the most skill trees (its own, Claude's, OpenCode's, `.agents` and plugin bundles) and shares bins/env/OS gating only with OpenClaw. It trails on per-skill tool restrictions (`allowed-tools` is inert), forked skills (`context: fork` is dormant), search beyond the prompt listing (OpenClaw's `skills_search`) and a registry. In served sessions only `$name` invokes a skill.

**Take-away.** For *running* sub-agents, candy-code edges out Claude Code: it adds pause, broadcast and a batch board to what both share. For *finding* them it is at parity: the model gets a fenced roster with descriptions and tools, `/agents` lists the full roster, and the web has a catalog panel; only `@agent` mentions and an agent wizard are missing.

### 4.5 Slash commands, palette, bang-shell

- **candy-code**:
  - 64 built-in command specs (57 slash commands + 7 palette/menu-only, +6 aliases), one spec file each, with a generated, drift-tested `docs/COMMANDS.md`.
  - Custom Markdown commands in `~/.candy-code/commands` and `<root>/.candy-code/commands`: `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1..$9`, gated `` !`cmd` ``, `@path`.
  - Foreign `.claude/commands` and `.opencode/command(s)` trees (project, home, `~/.config/opencode`) and plugin-bundle `commands/` import at the lowest precedence — they never shadow a built-in or native file — badged `[claude]`/`[opencode]`/`[bundle]` in the `/` popup. MCP prompts list as `/mcp__server__prompt`.
  - Ctrl+P palette: 49 rows — 42 of the 57 slash commands plus 7 palette-only actions — and provider/model/theme pickers; 15 argument-taking or read-out commands (`/effort`, `/loop`, `/fork`, `/review`, `/status`, …) and command files stay slash-only. F10 menu bar.
  - An unknown `/word` is refused locally, not sent to the model, so a typo costs no turn: the notice quotes the draft and offers a did-you-mean plus a skill-namesake pointer (`Chat::unknownSlashNotice`); because the `/` popup completes on Enter, the suggestion half fires mainly on the colon form (`/key:status`). A `/name` that a user-invocable skill claims is rewritten into the `$name` channel instead of refused.
  - Built-in shadowing is trust-gated: without `trustedProjectCommands` a project file cannot replace `/undo`, `/diff`, `/mcp` and the rest — refused attempts are reported at launch, and accepted shadows surface there as one aggregate row plus a `[user]`/`[project]` badge in the `/` popup; the 9 control-plane names remain never-file-overridable at any tier.
- **candy-code-web**: 57 built-ins listed; 41 run server-side, 16 refused as terminal-only (`/theme`, `/keys`, `/help`, `/sessions`, `/review`, …). Native, foreign and bundle command files list and run server-side, but a trusted project's built-in overrides apply only in the TUI; MCP prompts and `/skill-name` are TUI-only. `!cmd` runs on the server and its rows arrive as transcript events; a Ctrl+K palette lists sessions, panels and server-runnable commands.
- **Claude Code**: ~117 commands and bundled skills; custom commands merged into skills; MCP prompts become `/server:prompt`; typo suggestions. Messages typed during a turn are delivered *between tool calls*.
- **OpenCode**: ~33 built-ins; Markdown/JSON commands with `agent`, `model` and `subtask` frontmatter; MCP prompts and skills appear as commands; Ctrl+P palette over all actions.
- **OpenClaw**: ~60 core commands; skills double as commands (native menus on Discord/Telegram); ⌘K palette in the Control UI; no `` !`cmd` `` templating.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Events | 12 (Pre/PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, Pre/PostCompact, TaskCreated/Completed, TeammateIdle) | 33 | ~13 plugin hooks fire (`permission.ask` declared, never fired) | Internal hooks + ~40 typed plugin hooks |
| Kinds | Shell command only | command, http, mcp_tool, prompt (LLM), agent (experimental) | In-process JS/TS | In-process JS/TS |
| Payload | `CRUSH_*` env vars plus Claude-shaped JSON on stdin (session_id, cwd, hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_response) | JSON on stdin | function args | function args |
| Verdicts | exit 0 allow / 1-2 deny / 3 ask / 4 rewrite, **plus Claude Code's JSON envelope** | exit 2 block; JSON allow/deny/ask/defer, updatedInput, additionalContext | mutate / throw | block / rewrite / approve / claim |
| Failure | **Fails closed** (60 s) | `onFailure: block` opt-in | no timeout | per-hook timeouts, fail-closed gates |
| Claude-Code compat | 🟡 Reads `hooks` from `~/.claude/settings.json` and trusted project `.claude/settings(.local).json` (command type only — other types or newer entry keys refuse the launch); unknown events skipped and recorded; exit 1 denies where Claude Code proceeds | reference | ❌ (🔌 opencode-froggy) | ❌ detected, never run |
| UI | Verdicts in tool rows; `/hooks` read-only browser | `/hooks` read-only browser | toasts via plugins | `openclaw hooks list` |

### 4.7 MCP and how tools are exposed

- **candy-code**:
  - Covers tools, resources (`@mcp:` mentions) and prompts (`/mcp__server__prompt`) over stdio, Streamable HTTP (buffered replies, no GET stream) and legacy SSE (origin-locked), with a strong trust model: project `.mcp.json` sits behind `trustedProjectMcp` with per-server fingerprint pins, credential env vars are stripped, and `mcp list` never spawns servers.
  - Deferred loading per server: a server whose schemas exceed `mcp.lazySchemaTokens` (8000) is reached through `mcp_list`/`mcp_call`; smaller servers and `eager: true` entries keep first-class bridges. A preset's `mcpServers` allowlist strips its `mcp__` bridges but does not scope the `mcp_list`/`mcp_call` dispatchers.
  - User-level `~/.candy-code/mcp.json` plus project `.mcp.json` (project wins); missing: elicitation, sampling, roots, list_changed, answering server pings, runtime enable/disable and MCP-server mode.
  - OAuth is PKCE over a loopback listener (`candy-code mcp auth login`); the TUI's `/mcp login <server>` forks that flow and prints the URL, and `/mcp reconnect` restarts servers when the config is unchanged; tokens attach at the next launch.
  - HTTP tool-call timeouts are configurable per server (toolTimeout default 120 s).
- **candy-code-web**: MCP calls are generic cards; the Context panel lists project servers (transport, trust) and offers a trust prompt for an untrusted project; `/mcp` verbs answer as text; `@mcp:` mentions, MCP prompt commands and `/mcp login` are TUI-only.
- **Claude Code**:
  - Transports: stdio, SSE, HTTP and WebSocket.
  - OAuth, resources as `@server:` mentions, and prompts as commands; elicitation, but no sampling.
  - Five scopes (local, project, user, managed, plugin/connector).
  - **Tool search is on by default**, so only tool names enter context (also behind `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateways, which are retried without it on a 400/422; it falls back to upfront loading for older models and Azure-hosted Foundry).
  - `claude mcp serve` exposes Claude Code itself as a server.
  - Long tool calls move to the background after 2 minutes, and servers on protocol 2026-07-28 can run MCP tasks that outlive the session (public beta).
- **OpenCode**: stdio plus remote (HTTP, then SSE fallback); automatic OAuth on 401; resources via `@` and model tools; prompts as commands. No sampling or elicitation (disabled deliberately), and no deferred loading by default (an experimental code mode hides MCP tools behind one `execute` tool). v2 makes Code Mode the default, drops SSE, and supports elicitation; its forms render in TUI, desktop and web.
- **OpenClaw**:
  - stdio, SSE and HTTP with OAuth; resources and prompts as model-side tools.
  - Tool Search on by default (marked experimental) behind `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call`.
  - `openclaw mcp serve` exposes its channel conversations as a stdio MCP server, and `openclaw attach` gives Claude Code grant-scoped OpenClaw tools.

### 4.8 System prompt, per-turn reminders, prompt caching

- **candy-code**:
  - Up to 13 ordered slots: base (per model family) → maxims → tool guidance (incl. Task doctrine) → repo map → symbol map → user rules / personal AGENTS.md / ancestor / root / forced docs / project rules → `<project-memory>` → enabled skills → `<available-skills>` → plan-mode reminder → `<env>`.
  - Each step also gets a user-role `<turn-context>` tail: git status/diff after writes, changed-since-read files, instruction-file diffs, memory recall, context % past 60 %, post-compaction re-injection.
  - Byte-stability is engineered (per-session memo, volatile state in the tail).
  - Explicit cache breakpoints on the native `anthropic` arm and Claude-on-Vertex (`CacheBreakpoints`, ≤4 marks) and Bedrock (`cachePoint`); OpenAI and SGLang cache prefixes server-side; `CacheHealthWatch` warns on repeated zero-cache replies. Marks use the default 5-minute TTL and nothing keeps the cache warm.
  - No raw-prompt dump.
  - Harness text tells the model batching Task calls is sanctioned "even where project instructions advise running sub-agents one at a time", which ships into every project.
- **Claude Code**:
  - Three layers: system prompt (snapshotted once per conversation), project context (CLAUDE.md + memory reminder), conversation (append-only `<system-reminder>`s).
  - Git snapshot taken once at startup.
  - Deferred tools announced via reminders.
  - Idle compaction before the 1-hour cache expires (a `/config` toggle); on Pro/Max, resuming a long idle chat first estimates its share of the 5-hour limit.
- **OpenCode**: one system string rebuilt every step (agent prompt, `<env>`, references, instructions, MCP instructions, skills), collapsed to at most two system messages for caching; mode reminders as synthetic user parts.
- **OpenClaw**:
  - An OpenClaw-owned prompt with an explicit internal cache boundary (stable sections above, time/channel below).
  - Volatile runtime facts travel as user-role "Runtime Context" carriers.
  - Prompt snapshots are drift-checked in CI.

### 4.9 Context management and compaction

| | candy-code | Claude Code | OpenCode | OpenClaw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Counting | Script-weighted estimate calibrated against provider-reported usage; the 70/85/95 % tiers and the status bar read the same calibrated figure (system prompt, tool schemas and tool arguments included); the in-turn step budget is provider-anchored | Provider-reported | Provider-reported | Provider-reported |
| Auto trigger | Tiers 70/85/95 %, absolute caps 100k/150k, in-turn step budget, overflow retry; opt-in idle fold (`compaction.idleAuto`) after an hour idle | ≈ model limit (`/autocompact`); a standard-context session past 200K compacts and continues; idle compaction before cache expiry (`/config` toggle) | input limit − min(20k, maxOutput), mid-turn | window − reserve (16–20k); overflow; byte guard |
| Method | Model summary with six facets + merged `<session-state>`; summaries **pre-fetched ahead of need** using the cached prefix; `SummarySafeguard` audits headings, asks and identifiers (HOLD → heuristic fold); re-inject files, plan, skills, git, todos | Clear old tool outputs first, then summarise (asking again if the reply has no summary); re-inject CLAUDE.md, memory, plan, last 5 files, skill listing + invoked skills, git | Anchored 5-section summary, verbatim ≤15k recent tail | **Safeguard** mode audits headings, pending asks and identifiers and keeps history on a failed audit; a summary timeout commits a summary-less compaction |
| Model-driven pruning | ✅ `Prune` / `Compress` / `Recall` tools + ref tags | ❌ | 🔌 opencode-dynamic-context-pruning (1.x only); magic-context `ctx_reduce` on either major | ❌ (harness-side cache-TTL trim and Anthropic server-side clearing only) |
| Side questions | `/btw` (title model; served sessions refuse it while a turn runs) | `/btw` | ❌ (v2 adds `/btw`) | `/btw` |

### 4.10 Permissions and safety at a glance

- **candy-code**:
  - Six modes (default, accept-edits, plan, auto, dont-ask, bypass).
  - A shell-aware rule engine: allow must cover every segment; deny fires on any segment.
  - Strong path jail for file tools (Bash isn't jailed) and DNS-pinned SSRF guard; opt-in bubblewrap sandbox for Bash and PtyRun that fails closed.
  - Policy self-grant floor; approval modal with once / session / save / edit-scope / refuse-with-note / refuse-and-stop.
  - `PtyRun` is inside the permission model: its steps are rule/classifier/breaker/grant subjects, render in the modal, drive shell hooks and honour the bwrap sandbox.
  - Edit/Write/ApplyPatch approvals preview the diff and show full arguments, with `v` to expand.
  - Auto mode is a regex classifier (opt-in `autoReview` sends flagged calls and every unflagged non-read-only shell call to the LLM reviewer; Edit/Write/WebFetch stay classifier-only).
  - `-p` defaults to bypass (with a notice on stderr) and enforces its spend cap; rules live in the user tier only; no TUI workspace-trust dialog; no managed policy.
- **candy-code-web**: server-wide approvals drawer (once / always-for-session / reject / reject & stop, with Edit/Write diff preview, AskUser choice buttons and Markdown plan approval); a read-only Rules panel (mode, rules, session grants); a project `.mcp.json` trust prompt in the Context panel; `remember: "user"` is not offered over the wire.
- **Claude Code**: **auto mode is the default starting mode since 2.1.283** for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions on supported models (classifier: server-side review, else a client-side model selectable with `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL`; falls back to prompts after 3 consecutive / 20 total blocks); `claude -p` and SDK runs with no mode set start in Manual; protected paths; OS sandbox with network-proxy allowlists; managed policy; diff in the approval prompt.
- **OpenCode**: permissive defaults (only external dirs, `*.env` and doom-loops ask); tree-sitter bash parsing; diff in the ask dialog; "always" approvals lost on restart; no sandbox, no trust dialog. v2 persists approvals per project (editable through its API) but allows external directories by default and drops the doom-loop guard.
- **OpenClaw**: **no sandbox and full host exec by default**; four session permission modes incl. an LLM exec reviewer; Docker/Podman/SSH sandboxes; approvals from phone or chat buttons; edits never approval-gated.

### 4.11 Startup screen, status, notifications

- **candy-code**:
  - A fresh launch shows the StartupSummary: version, provider · model, permission mode, cwd · branch, loaded instruction files, memory/skill/MCP counts and a tip.
  - Status bar: context %, cache share/age, mode, model.
  - `?` overlay generated from the live key registry.
  - Settings view showing source and apply mode per key.
  - Opt-in `notify`: terminal bell or OSC 9 desktop notification.
  - The startup terminal probe runs after raw-mode entry, so capability detection adds no visible delay and leaks no reply bytes.
  - The configured `statusLine` command runs off the UI thread in a forked child.
- **candy-code-web**: dashboard (served root, open questions, recent sessions, versions); sessions sidebar with question badges, tab-title counts, opt-in desktop notifications and polite live-region announcements; status bar (step, tokens, spend, mode select, model select, Compact button); About modal over `server.info` + `server.health`.
- **Claude Code**: welcome banner (version, model + effort, account, cwd, tips, announcements); spinner with elapsed time and token count; scriptable status line fed JSON; desktop notifications in Ghostty/Kitty/iTerm2; Remote Control push.
- **OpenCode**: logo + rotating tips + footer (`dir:branch`, MCP count, version); sidebar with context %, cost, MCP/LSP status, todos, modified files.
- **OpenClaw**: TUI header (gateway URL / agent / session); the Control UI is the real surface (context ring, plan-usage bars, activity recaps).

### 4.12 Surfaces

- **candy-code**: TUI, `-p` headless, `serve` (the `candy-code.v1` WebSocket protocol, 69 methods and 35 event types, plus the browser UI), `attach` (TUI over WS, redials and resumes from its cursor), `acp` (Zed / JetBrains / Neovim). No VS Code extension, desktop app, mobile app, chat channels or cloud execution.
- **candy-code-web**: multi-session cockpit (tabs + live 3×3 grid), server-wide approvals drawer, ten side panels (agents, todo, background, workflows, memory, rules, agent catalog, changes, context, generate), settings with provenance. Requests 61 of the 69 protocol methods (`server.shutdown` arrives as a notification and is handled).
- **Claude Code**: CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Desktop (Linux in beta), web (claude.ai/code), mobile (cloud sessions + Remote Control), Slack and Claude Tag, Chrome, channel plugins, `claude-cli://` deep links.
- **OpenCode**: one server, many clients (TUI, web, desktop, VS Code extension, ACP, SDK, GitHub/GitLab bots, `attach`); v2 adds a per-user background service, password-protected web, `opencode pair` links/QR, OpenTunnel and an iOS app, but its CLI has no GitHub bot.
- **OpenClaw**: always-on Gateway with 20+ chat channels, Control UI (a full agent IDE), TUI, macOS/Windows/iOS/Android apps, ACP, an OpenAI-compatible API.

## 5. What changed upstream since the last compile

### 5.1 OpenCode 1.19.4 → 2.1.4: what changes in the comparison

The "OpenCode 1.19.4" column in §3 and the OpenCode cells in §4 describe the 1.x line. This host runs 1.18.35, which differs from 1.19.4 only in:
- update behaviour;
- session sharing, which is gone on both (the share host answers 410);
- reasoning-variant generation;
- the bundled Bun.

Upstream ships two maintained lines from one repo:
- **v1:** npm `opencode-ai`, `latest` = 1.19.4 (also GitHub's "Latest" release).
  - 1.19.x stays on 1.x: update checks read only `opencode-ai@latest`, the curl script refuses 2.x, and updates are notify-only.
  - `/update` and `opencode upgrade --major` are the explicit routes to v2.
- **v2:** npm `@opencode/cli`, `latest` = 2.1.4.
  - Install with `curl …/v2/install`, `npm i -g @opencode/cli`, the `anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2` tap, mise, or `brew install opencode`: the Homebrew core formula ships v2. The v2 installer *replaces* the v1 binary.
  - v2 publishes release notes in the repo `CHANGELOG.md` and at opencode.ai/changelog, not as GitHub releases.
  - 2.1 renamed parts of the SDK, HTTP and plugin contracts: provider replay data moved to `native`, and summary compactions reference kept messages by `keepID`.

In the 2.1.4 column, **246 rows carry Δ and 76 of them have a different status code from 1.19.4**, which is why it gets its own column.

**What v2 gains (relevant to candy-code):**
- **Durable prompt inbox.** Typing while busy steers at the next step, as in v1. v2 adds an explicit queue-until-idle (leader+Enter) and makes the inbox durable. Execution is crash-recoverable through write-ahead claims under one per-user background service that every client attaches to (TUI, web, desktop, iOS, ACP).
- **Cache-stable instructions.** A frozen per-session baseline. Later AGENTS.md edits reach the model as a **unified diff message** ("The instructions from X changed. Here's the diff:"). MCP instructions, skills and references are also sent as changed entries only. The TUI shows "Instructions updated" / "Loaded <file>" rows, but not their content.
- **MCP through Code Mode by default.** One `execute` sandbox tool with budgeted one-line signatures, so full schemas aren't sent every request.
  - MCP **elicitation** forms (text, number, choice, multiselect, boolean, URL) render in the TUI, desktop and web.
  - An experimental client-MCP transport lets a UI client serve its own tools to the agent.
- **Built in:**
  - background shell and background sub-agents;
  - worktree tools;
  - `/btw`;
  - session tabs;
  - output-limit auto-continuation;
  - cache warming;
  - provider-native (OpenAI Responses) compaction;
  - whole-conversation summaries that reuse the prompt cache, with an optional `agents.compaction.model`;
  - session archiving;
  - PDF prompt attachments;
  - persistent PTY terminals, Windows included.
- **Experimental, off by default:**
  - background ("ahead-of-need") compaction;
  - the `todowrite` tool and todo panel;
  - TUI tools that let the agent open and type into the session terminal (write-only);
  - an SDK realtime-voice API.
- **Permissions.** Persisted per-project "Allow always" grants, listable, editable and deletable through `/api/permission/saved`. A working `permission.evaluate` plugin hook (v1's `permission.ask` never fired). Org policies, with Console-managed policies outranking everything.
- **Remote access.** Password-protected web by default, one-time `opencode pair` links / QR codes, OpenTunnel end-to-end remote, and an iOS app.

**What v2 removes or regresses (at 2.1.4):**
- **Instructions:** no CLAUDE.md fallback at all (AGENTS.md only; discovery walks up to `$HOME`).
- **Code intelligence and tasks:** no LSP (no diagnostics, no lsp tool; `lsp` config is accepted but inert) and no structured output. The todo tool exists only behind `experimental.todo`, without v1's priority field.
- **Commands and MCP:**
  - no `@file` in command templates;
  - skills are no longer slash commands (load them with `@skill-id`);
  - no pruning options (`compaction.prune`/`tail_turns` are ignored);
  - no SSE MCP transport;
  - no `opencode agent create` wizard;
  - no `opencode github` / `opencode pr` (the repo's GitHub Action installs v1 and runs `opencode github run`).
- **Prompts and editing:**
  - per-agent temperature/top_p in `request.body` is accepted but not sent; set them on a model variant instead;
  - models without an override, Gemini included, get a 15-line generic prompt (gpt/astra/kimi/trinity/meta and Anthropic keep theirs);
  - the fuzzy edit chain is two fallbacks (typographic variants, then trailing whitespace) instead of nine replacers.
- **Permissions:** `external_directory` is *allowed* by default; there is no doom-loop guard; sub-agents use their own rules instead of inheriting the parent's denies.
- **Sharing:** gone on both lines (2.0.30 and 1.19.1), so it does not separate them.

**Plugins.** V1 plugin implementations don't run on v2, but much of the ecosystem ships v2 builds:
- **Run on v2:**
  - opencode-agent-memory 0.3.0 (v2 only)
  - opencode-goal-plugin 0.11+ (both majors; its author verified 2.0.16–2.0.31)
  - @plannotator/opencode (both)
  - opencode-supermemory 2.0.17 (both)
  - @cortexkit/opencode-magic-context (both: `ctx_reduce` pruning, hybrid recall, an overnight "dreamer")
  - opencode-froggy 1.6 (Claude-Code-style hooks)
  - opencode-handoff 0.6 (v2 ≥2.1.2 only)
- **Partial:** opencode-pty 0.4.0 has an `opencode-pty/v2` entry that registers only its web-UI commands, none of the `pty_*` agent tools; oh-my-openagent 5.1.48 loads on v2 with its agents, tools and hooks inactive.
- **V1-only:** DCP 3.2.0, subtask2, opencode-conductor-plugin, opencode-scheduler, opencode-gpt-imagegen, harness-memory.

**Effect on the candy-code comparison:**
- **Where v2 catches up with candy-code:**
  - cache-stable instructions (frozen baseline plus diffs);
  - a detachable background service (WEB-N4 ❌→✅) and durable event replay (WEB-N3 🟡→✅);
  - ahead-of-need compaction (CTX-N1, experimental);
  - a configurable summary model (MOD-13);
  - PDF attachments (MOD-22);
  - model-driven pruning, memory consolidation and goal mode through plugins that run on v2.
- **Where v2 pulls further ahead of candy-code:**
  - the push transport around background work (output streamed to a managed file with a completion notification, versus candy-code's poll-`ShellOutput` loop);
  - the single-`execute` Code Mode packaging;
  - MCP elicitation forms in every client, including the browser (candy-code has no elicitation or sampling);
  - client-hosted tools;
  - built-in remote pairing and tunnel (candy-code signs in by token and attaches, but has no pair/QR/tunnel).

  candy-code has background shell and deferred MCP loading itself: `Bash run_in_background` over a `BackgroundShellRegistry` with `ShellOutput`/`ShellStop`, and `mcp_list`/`mcp_call` deferral.
- **Where v2 falls further behind candy-code:**
  - no LSP;
  - no structured output (candy-code has `--json-schema`);
  - no CLAUDE.md;
  - a permissive external-dir default;
  - no doom-loop guard;
  - todos off by default;
  - PTY driving only as a blind, experimental write (candy-code's `PtyRun` reads output).

**Host-specific notes:**
- **Installed copy.** 1.18.35 (curl install at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`); v2 is not installed. With `autoupdate: true` the binary has stayed on 1.18.35; on 1.19.x the same setting only notifies.
- **Plugin pins for v1.** v1 resolves an unpinned or `@latest` plugin once and reuses `~/.cache/opencode/packages/<spec>` while that directory exists, so it keeps loading the cached `opencode-agent-memory` 0.2.0 even though `@latest` is the v2-only 0.3.0. The same holds for `opencode-handoff` (cached 0.5.0; `@latest` 0.6.1 needs OpenCode ≥2.1.2). Both break only if that cache is cleared or the config moves to a fresh machine. Pinning `opencode-agent-memory@0.2.0` and `opencode-handoff@0.5.0` is a cheap safeguard for v1. v2 keeps a separate cache (`~/.cache/opencode/npm/`) and would fetch the v2 builds.
- **v2 config migration.**
  - It would ignore `subagent_depth: 4` (moved to `experimental.subagent_depth`), make `lsp: true` and the `lsp` permission entries inert, and map `autoupdate: true` to `update: "auto"`.
  - Of the 11 global plugin entries, only plannotator, agent-memory and handoff would run.
  - opencode-pty would need the `opencode-pty/v2` spec and would give the agent no PTY tools.
  - DCP (global `@latest` and this repo's pinned `@3.1.3`), subtask2 and conductor would not run.
- **Large first-start import.** On first start, v2 would import the v1 session store, `opencode.db`, 11.7 GB here.

### 5.2 Claude Code 2.1.302 → 2.1.311

Ten releases (2.1.302–2.1.311; 2.1.303 and 2.1.308 are fixes only, 2.1.306 has two fixes) of hardening and consistency work, with no new product surface. One status code moved, CMD-12, and four 🆕 rows describe Claude Code features found in this range.
- **Per-command keybindings (CMD-12 ✅).** The `command:<name>` keybinding action runs `/<name>` from a key; key-bound slash commands do not fire in `!` mode (2.1.309).
- **Long-running MCP calls (🆕 MCP-N2).** MCP tasks are in public beta in the CLI, SDK and GitHub Actions (2.1.304) and can outlive the session; long MCP tool calls move to the background after 2 minutes. Tool search is on by default behind a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, retried without it on a 400/422 (MCP-12).
- **Usage-optimisation advice (🆕 OBS-N1).** `/usage` attributes plan usage to skills, subagents, plugins and MCP servers, and its warnings are one-line fixes that `f` applies (2.1.305); the same fixes appear in VS Code and `/doctor`.
- **Deep links and plugin hints (🆕 WEB-N6, PLG-N3).** `claude-cli://` links open a local session in a given directory with the prompt pre-filled, never auto-sent; marketplace `relevance` signals and CLI hint tags trigger plugin install suggestions.
- **Headless default (PER-01, AUT-01).** `claude -p` and SDK runs with no permission mode start in Manual (2.1.302); interactive terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode.
- **Auto-mode classifier (PER-07).** `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` picks the client-side classifier model, and server-side review compacts conversations too long to check (2.1.302); `/auto-mode-setup` works on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry (2.1.304).
- **Fork subagents (AGT-09, AGT-10, AGT-13).** On by default in `-p`, the SDK, desktop and VS Code (2.1.302); concurrent forks are told which launch is theirs (2.1.307); subagents can use MCP servers that finish connecting after they start (2.1.311).
- **Nested instruction cap (INS-08, INS-18).** A nested CLAUDE.md or on-demand rules file over a per-file cap loads only its start, with a Read pointer (2.1.309).
- **Compaction (CTX-03, CTX-05, CTX-13, CTX-N2).** A standard-context session past 200K compacts and continues, and compaction asks again when the reply has no summary (2.1.311); `/config` has an idle-compaction row (2.1.302); on Pro/Max a "Resume this conversation?" dialog estimates the share of the 5-hour limit a resume would use (2.1.304).
- **Models (MOD-10, MOD-15, MOD-18).** In the terminal on Anthropic's API, `ultrathink` runs its turn at xhigh effort on the 5.5 models and Fable 5.1 (2.1.311); Bedrock, Mantle, Vertex and Foundry load model settings from a signed catalog on downloads.claude.ai (2.1.311); an unparseable tool call is retried up to twice (2.1.307).
- **Shell and Monitor (SH-03, TL-10).** The Monitor tool and plugin monitors work on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry (2.1.310); a shell command that reaches its timeout returns its output so far and keeps running in the background (2.1.311).
- **Telemetry (OBS-02, PER-14).** The OTel event `claude_code.safety_event` logs every tool call that a rule, auto mode, a safety check, a hook or the sandbox refuses or prompts (2.1.307); `tool_decision` carries agent and request ids (2.1.310).
- **Sandbox and permission hardening (SH-06, PER-03, PER-08).** Shell startup files run inside the sandbox, `Edit(path)` denies beat subshell redirects, and worktree isolation refuses locale-prefixed escapes (2.1.309); `sandbox.allowNestedUserNamespaces` lets Chromium or rootless podman nest user namespaces on Linux (2.1.305).
- **Unchanged.** 33 hook events and five handler kinds; MCP elicitation but no sampling; 315 official marketplace entries; 20 bundled skills; auto memory without consolidation; agent teams behind an experimental flag.

### 5.3 OpenClaw 2026.9.9 → 2026.10.7

Eight stable releases (there is no 2026.10.0). 2026.10.5 is the feature release and 10.1 has a smaller change set; the others add models and reliability fixes, with 10.6 a security patch and 10.7 a small patch. No OpenClaw status code moved; three 🆕 rows describe its new features.
- **Self-learning skills (🆕 SKL-N1, SKL-14).** Skill Workshop 2.0 (10.5): the agent saves and patches learned skills directly, with change history, saved versions, Undo, archive and restore, and auto-archive of skills unused for 30 days. The proposal queue and `workshop evaluate/apply` are gone.
- **Skill search (🆕 SKL-N2, SKL-04, SKL-05, PRM-06).** `skills_search` and `skills_read` tools (10.5): the prompt carries a bounded skill directory, and the model can search the skills it omits.
- **Process inspector (🆕 SH-N2, AGT-12, UI-19).** Control UI Subagents and Processes side panels with per-item Stop (10.5).
- **CLAUDE.md (INS-01, HK-07).** Managed Claude CLI turns use OpenClaw's tool surface and do not load Claude user settings, `CLAUDE.md` and rules, auto-memory, user hooks and plugins, or Claude-only MCP servers (10.7).
- **Doom-loop stop (TL-N2).** Three consecutive identical tool errors always end the turn (10.5).
- **Compaction and continuation (CTX-05, CTX-N4).** Automatic compaction continues after a summary timeout, dropping older unsummarized context (10.5); agents continue unfinished tool work after an empty length-limited reply (10.7); `agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPrecheck` is an opt-in check (10.6).
- **Sharing and channels (SES-09, WEB-09).** Public conversation links at the normal chat URL, readable anonymously, and a bundled X/Twitter channel with guest mode (10.5).
- **Editing and worktrees (TL-05, GIT-08, AGT-18).** A multi-file `apply_patch` validates every target before changing any (10.7); managed worktrees have a global cap (`worktreeMaxCount`, default 4096) with eviction and background gc (10.5).
- **Runtime (PLAT-01, PLAT-05).** The Node floor is 24.22.1 / 26.12.1 (10.6); installations are sealed immutable generations with activation and recovery (10.1); npm `extended-stable` is the Gateway-only LTS line 2026.9.34.
- **Other 10.1 changes.** Code Mode `store`/`load` values persist across cells and restarts (TL-N3); a Workboard sidebar; MCP Apps can call their tools while their views stay open; the selected memory plugin owns the pre-compaction flush (MEM-15).
- **Models (MOD-03).** Haiku 5.5 (9.9), GPT-6.1 Sol in the Codex list, and Gemini 4 Argon and Gemini 3.8 Flash (10.5).

## 6. How candy-code and candy-code-web can improve (prioritised)

Project policy applies throughout: **wire dormant code instead of deleting it**, fix root causes rather than "disable + TODO", and never add a blanket total-request timeout to LLM calls. Many of the open items below are *wiring* jobs:
- **Dormant or half-wired:** the fork-skill executor `App::dispatchSkill` and the skill asset loader have no caller; `McpClient::setAgentPreset()` has no caller; a preset's `memory:` key is parsed and inert; the sugar-forms `TextObject` resolver is unwired; the TUI receives `ToolProgress` frames but never paints them; `serve` arms the runtime-notice sink but never drains it; the web computes `canGenerateVideo` and never reads it.
- **Live but used narrowly:** `SecretRedactor` covers memory, the journal, dreams, the audit log and `/share`, but streamed tool output stays raw; `ExecReviewer` runs only under opt-in `autoReview`.

### 6.1 Fix first: served-session parity and correctness

1. **Served sessions drop runtime notices.** Nothing drains the `RuntimeNoticeSink` that `serve` arms, so the browser never sees the "Recalled N notes" row, a fallback-model switch or any other mid-turn runtime warning (MOD-14, MEM-10).
2. **Served sessions skip turn-end work.** Auto-memory consolidation, the dream pass, prompt suggestions and `autoCommit: turn` commits are scheduled only from the TUI's turn completion (MEM-02, MEM-08, UI-34, GIT-02).
3. **`/loop` never fires on serve.** `ScheduleRegistry::fireDue()` skips ephemeral rows on serve and only the TUI pumps them, so a browser `/loop` answers "registered" and never runs (AUT-08).
4. **A Claude settings file can refuse the launch.** A non-`command` hook type, or an entry key beyond type/command/timeout (`async`, `statusMessage`, `if`), in `~/.claude/settings.json` (always read) or a trusted project's `.claude/settings(.local).json` refuses the whole launch instead of skipping that entry; exit 1 denies where Claude Code proceeds (HK-07).
5. **A preset's `mcpServers` does not scope deferred MCP.** It strips the preset's `mcp__` bridges, but `mcp_list`/`mcp_call` still reach every deferred server (MCP-11).
6. **Trusted command overrides are TUI-only.** Served sessions and `command.list` load commands without `projectCommandsTrusted`, so a trusted project's built-in override applies in the TUI only (CMD-02).
7. **Read images break in the web.** A Read image becomes a MediaCard whose `media.fetch` cannot serve it, because that method reads only the session media store (TL-19).
8. **Served sessions refuse `/btw` mid-turn.** `SessionHost::runCommand` refuses every built-in except workflow controls while a turn runs (CTX-11).
9. **Telemetry covers the TUI only.** OTLP export rides the `chat()` path; headless `-p` builds no Chat and `serve` mounts no sink (OBS-02).

### 6.2 Make what already exists visible (mostly wiring)

The engine computes more than either client shows. Each competitor shows *something* here: Claude Code's "Saved/Recalled N memories" rows link the files, OpenClaw's Control UI has Subagents and Processes panels, and OpenCode v2 prints "Instructions updated" rows.
- **TUI:** paint the live shell tail it already receives (SH-08); a user-facing list of background shells beside the model's `ShellOutput`/`ShellStop` (SH-N2); a hook log view (HK-08); a raw request or system-prompt dump (PRM-15); recall rows that name the recalled notes rather than count them (MEM-10).
- **Web:** a startup summary of the loaded instruction files (INS-14); notices when nested instruction files load or instructions change (INS-08, INS-12); rule packs and the `[claude]`/`[opencode]`/`[bundle]` origin badges in the Context panel and `/` completion (INS-03, SKL-03, CMD-10, CMD-N1); gated-out skills and the reason (SKL-12); MCP server liveness and the user tier (MCP-01, MCP-10); cache tokens and model retries (MOD-18, MOD-19).

### 6.3 Context, prompt and memory

- **Memory:** no per-sub-agent memory, since the preset `memory:` key is inert and the agent scope never reaches the prompt (MEM-13); `/memory import` lands in that non-prompt scope and there is no export (MEM-14); no daily log (MEM-11); past-session summaries are not searchable by the model (MEM-12); no standing intents (MEM-N3).
- **Instructions:** no managed-policy instruction file (INS-06), no instruction-file trust gate (INS-19) and no in-app editor or `#` quick-add for instruction files (INS-16); `instructions` globs are repo-relative, with no URLs (INS-11); no project references beyond one `--root` (PRM-N2).
- **Prompt:** no system-prompt override or append flag (PRM-09) and no output styles (PRM-10); the `<env>` date is frozen at session start and there is no knowledge-cutoff note (PRM-14).
- **Caching:** cache marks use the default 5-minute TTL and nothing keeps the cache warm across idle gaps (MOD-N3).
- **Skills:** the roster is read once at launch (SKL-13); skills past `skills.listingMaxBytes` collapse to an "N more" line with no search tool (SKL-N2).

### 6.4 Interop: cheap wins for people arriving from Claude Code or OpenCode

- **Hooks:** skip and record a non-`command` hook type or an unknown entry key instead of refusing the launch, and match Claude Code's exit-1 semantics (HK-07); hooks are shell commands only, with no HTTP, prompt or agent kinds (HK-03).
- **Skills:** honour `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` (SKL-11) and `context: fork` (SKL-15); accept `/skill-name` in served sessions (SKL-06).
- **Commands:** the `model`, `subtask`, `allowed-tools` and `agent` frontmatter keys are inert (CMD-04); bundle commands have no `/plugin:name` namespace (CMD-10).
- **Instruction files:** `.windsurfrules` and `CONVENTIONS.md` are not read (INS-03).
- **Config:** no settings or permission-rule import (CFG-08); `mcp import` prints a translated block and writes nothing (MCP-15).
- **Agents:** no `@agent` mention (AGT-20) and no creation wizard (AGT-07).

### 6.5 Breadth gaps (new capability)

| Area | Gap vs competitors | Suggested approach |
|---|---|---|
| MCP | No elicitation (OpenCode 2.1.4 renders forms in TUI, desktop and web), sampling, roots, logging or list_changed, and server pings go unanswered; no GET stream on Streamable HTTP; no MCP-server mode; no runtime enable/disable; no MCP tasks or auto-backgrounded calls; image and audio parts reach the model only as descriptions | Handle server-initiated frames in sugar-mcp-client; `mcp serve` over the tool catalog; pass image parts through on vision wires |
| Plugins / marketplace | Bundles carry content only (skills, commands, agents); no registry or marketplace, no code-defined tools in the shipped binary, no in-process plugin or mod API, no install recommendations (Claude Code: 315-entry marketplace; OpenCode: npm plugins; OpenClaw: ClawHub) | A `marketplace.json` index over `bundles install`; file-defined script tools through the exec gate |
| Providers | No native subscription OAuth (`candy-code login` hands off to `claude`/`codex`), no OpenAI Responses API, no Azure/Foundry or OpenRouter type, no OS keychain, no fast mode or service tier, no audio input or output, no advisor tool | A Responses arm beside Chat Completions; first-class `azure` and `openrouter` types over the OpenAI wire; a keychain-backed credential store |
| Automation | No outbound webhooks; no model-callable schedule tool; no heartbeat that reaches the user off-terminal; no packaged SDK; no PR-comment or issue-triage bot | A `Schedule` tool over the existing `ScheduleRegistry`; outbound webhooks on the typed event DTOs |
| Shell & tools | PDFs and tool-result images reach the model natively only on Anthropic and Vertex-Claude wires (elsewhere a `pdftotext` hint or a caption); WebFetch returns raw HTML; WebSearch needs a user SearXNG endpoint; no notebook, browser-control, code-mode, external code-search, canvas or computer-use tool; no persistent shell; no network allowlist; the tool list is the same in every mode | Document blocks for Read on supporting providers; HTML→Markdown in WebFetch; a domain allowlist in the bwrap `no-network` mode |
| Editing | Auto-format and LSP auto-detect are opt-in, with no bundled formatter table (OpenCode ships 26) and no LSP auto-install; no BOM handling; no live file watcher | Default formatter table gated on binary presence (LspLauncher's probe seam); BOM inherit beside `IndentShift::inheritEndings` |
| Git / review | No `/commit` or PR tooling; no main-session worktree; no review pane (`/diff` posts a fenced diff) | A worktree flag for the main session; a review pane over the checkpoint refs |
| Sessions | No session import, incognito sessions or peer messaging between independent sessions; no push of a local session to another device; one live session per TUI window | Import the JSON export; an ephemeral flag that skips the session store and auto-memory |
| Observability | No insights or usage attribution across sessions (Claude Code's `/usage` attributes and recommends fixes); no JSONL transcripts; no live diagnostics capture | Mount the OTLP sink on serve and `-p`; per-skill/agent/MCP attribution over `usage_records` |
| Distribution & surfaces | No brew, npm, curl installer or native binary; Linux-first, macOS best-effort, no Windows; only `lang/en.php` ships; no VS Code extension, desktop, mobile, chat-channel, cloud or voice surface; no built-in TLS for remote use | — |
| Permissions | Rules in the user tier only; no managed policy; a regex auto classifier with an opt-in LLM reviewer; tool output not redacted and MCP output not tagged untrusted; no restricted-mode flag; session grants are revoked only by typing `/permissions revoke` (no edit, no Rules-panel control) and config-saved rules only by editing the file; no general workspace-trust dialog | Project and session rule tiers behind trust; revoke and edit controls in the Rules panel over the existing `/permissions revoke` effect |

### 6.6 TUI polish

- **Composer:** vim counts, text objects, `cw`, named registers and line-wise `V` (the composer aliases `V` to `v`) (UI-07); a copy-reply/copy-code command (UI-16); edit-and-resubmit of an earlier message (UI-15); stripping invisible Unicode before send (UI-N5); key bindings for slash and custom commands (CMD-12); argument-taking and file commands in the Ctrl+P palette (CMD-08).
- **Transcript and feedback:** a live shell tail (SH-08); transcript search (UI-18); a one-key compact/verbose toggle (UI-32); a recap after inactivity (UI-N4).
- **Look and access:** session JSON on `statusLine` stdin (UI-23); custom theme files (UI-02); a highlighter beyond 4 token classes in 8 languages (UI-04); side-by-side diffs (UI-05); a screen-reader mode (UI-30); a first-run setup wizard (UI-29).

### 6.7 candy-code-web

1. **Served-session parity** (6.1 items 1–3 and 6–8): drain the notice sink, run turn-end memory work, pump ephemeral `/loop` rows, honour trusted command overrides, serve Read images and allow `/btw` mid-turn.
2. **Host bodies for refused built-ins.** 16 built-ins are refused `ui_only`: `/new`, `/sessions`, `/effort`, `/exit`, `/theme`, `/settings`, `/keys`, `/help`, `/compress`, `/newrule`, `/pane`, `/layout`, `/editor`, `/budget`, `/review` and `/security-review`. The material ones are `/review`, `/security-review` (GIT-10), `/effort` (MOD-15) and `/budget`.
3. **Callers for the unrequested methods.** The web requests 61 of the 69 protocol methods. Still uncalled: `files.read`; `memory.log` and `memory.undo` (a memory-history view, MEM-N1); `session.share` and `session.unshare` (a Share button, SES-09); `workflow.status`; and `workspace.close` (closing a root host, WEB-N2). `server.shutdown` is Admin-scope and arrives as a handled notification.
4. **TUI-only features to bring over:** `/skill-name`, MCP prompt commands, `@mcp:` resources and the `/mcp login` fork; img2img, inpaint and video in the Generate panel (UI-N3); interactive stdin to a running command (SH-05); `watchFiles` AI-comment prompts on served sessions (EDT-N2).
5. **Missing views:** a help/shortcuts overlay (UI-28); a hooks panel (HK-10); a usage page (OBS-03); a permission audit view (PER-14) and rule editor (PER-03); a schedules panel (AUT-07); a background-shell list with kill (SH-N2); a team-board view (AGT-N1); a server log view (OBS-01); a per-turn or checkpoint diff view (GIT-09); `serve` status, stop and logs (WEB-N4).
6. **Composer and transcript:** copy buttons (UI-16); drag-drop and PDF upload (UI-12, MOD-22); reverse history search (UI-09); large-paste collapse (UI-11); edit-and-resubmit (UI-15); a global thinking toggle (UI-22) and compact/verbose toggle (UI-32); an elapsed-time counter (UI-31); prompt suggestions (UI-34); keybinding customisation (UI-25); branch display (GIT-01); Edit/Write asks with file context and ApplyPatch asks rendered as diffs (EDT-03).
7. **i18n** of the web chrome from the server `Lang` catalogue (PLAT-10; backlog).
8. **Ideas from the competitors:**
   - OpenCode v2's pairing links / QR codes and end-to-end tunnel for phone access, and its browser-rendered MCP elicitation forms;
   - Claude Code's Remote Control push notifications;
   - OpenClaw's Control UI side panels (Files, Terminal, Review, Subagents and Processes; the Changes panel partly covers Review), PR chips with CI status, and approvals answerable from chat apps.

## Appendix A — Per-feature detail (how, when, where, evidence)

Every cell of the matrix in §3 is expanded below with its full detail and evidence, grouped by category; click a row to expand it. candy-code citations are repo-relative to `candy-code/` (`web:` and `candy-code-web/` paths point into the web client) on monorepo `master`. Competitor citations point to the installed package, the source tags or npm tarballs examined, or official doc pages.

### PLAT — Platform & distribution

<details><summary><b>PLAT-01</b> Implementation language / runtime</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — Runs on stock php-cli 8.3. composer.json requires ext-sqlite3, pdo_sqlite, mbstring and intl, and suggests curl plus pcntl/posix/ffi, which `serve` needs. `doctor` opens a real sqlite3 and PDO handle and fails when either is missing. Interactive turns run in a pcntl-forked child streaming frames to the parent; without pcntl they run in-process and the screen updates only when they finish. — _Evidence:_ `composer.json:35-39,77-81`; `src/Cli/Subcommands.php:261-271`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — `src-web/` holds the TS (kept out of the PSR-4 `src/`). Deps: @tanstack/vue-virtual (transcript), markdown-it + DOMPurify (rendering). A one-class PHP shim `SugarCraft\CodeWeb\Assets` tells `serve` where `dist/` is. Node is only needed to develop, never to run. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/package.json`; `candy-code-web/src/Assets.php`; `candy-code-web/README.md`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — The native installer keeps versioned binaries under `~/.local/share/claude/versions/` with a launcher symlink at `~/.local/bin/claude` (observed: ELF x86-64; 2.1.311 = 293,776,752 bytes, `du` 281M; the binary embeds Bun v1.4.4). The npm package `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` is a supported install path and runs under Node (npm `latest` 2.1.311, `stable` 2.1.308). Bundles ripgrep; on macOS/Linux/WSL the shell's `find`/`grep` are embedded `bfs`/`ugrep`. The Agent SDK (TS/Python) drives the same CLI as a subprocess. — _Evidence:_ local: `ls -la ~/.local/share/claude/versions/`, `du -sh …/2.1.311`, `file ~/.local/bin/claude`, `grep -a 'Bun v1.'`; `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code dist-tags`; cc:setup; cc:tools-reference#glob-tool-behavior
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — v1 layout: `packages/opencode` holds the agent loop and HTTP server, `packages/tui` the OpenTUI/Solid terminal client, `packages/core` the shared Effect services (plus the unused v2 runner), `packages/app` the web/desktop UI, and `packages/desktop` the Electron 42 shell. The npm package `opencode-ai` installs a per-platform prebuilt binary (~215 MB, bundling Bun 1.4.4). Tree-sitter WASM is used for bash parsing and syntax highlighting. — _Evidence:_ `npm view opencode-linux-x64@1.19.4 dist.unpackedSize` = 214522169; packages/desktop/package.json (`electron 42.3.3`); tag v1.19.4
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — Same architecture as 1.x re-cut into packages/core (Location-scoped services, durable session inbox, plugin host), packages/server, packages/cli, packages/tui (OpenTUI/Solid), packages/app + desktop (Electron), packages/ai (own provider protocols; AI-SDK packages still usable via `aisdk:` prefix) and packages/sdk (in-process host incl. Cloudflare workerd). The linux-x64 platform package is 240.4 MB unpacked and bundles Bun 1.4.4. — _Evidence:_ `npm view @opencode/cli-linux-x64@2.1.4 dist.unpackedSize` = 240417179; opencode.ai/changelog v2.1.3; tag v2.1.4 packages/
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Gateway, CLI, TUI and the embedded agent runtime ship as the `openclaw` npm package (ESM bundles). `engines.node` is `>=24.22.1 <25` or `>=26.12.1`; Node 26 is recommended and Bun 1.4+ is opt-in, while fresh Linux-companion setups and the macOS app run the Gateway on a bundled OpenClaw Bun fork. Companion apps: macOS menu-bar, iOS/watchOS, Android, Windows Hub (WinUI), Linux companion; the Control UI is a Vite + Lit SPA. — _Evidence:_ `oc@2026.10.7/package.json` (engines); `oc@2026.10.7/docs/install/index.md`; `oc@2026.10.7/docs/platforms/linux.md` (Use the bundled runtime)

</details>

- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Channels: `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install` piped to bash, `npm i -g opencode-ai` (bun/pnpm/yarn too), `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode` (recommended over core brew), `pacman -S opencode` / `paru -S opencode-bin`, `choco`, `scoop`, `mise use -g github:anomalyco/opencode`, `docker run ghcr.io/anomalyco/opencode`, and GitHub release binaries. `opencode upgrade --method` accepts curl/npm/pnpm/bun/brew/choco/scoop. — _Evidence:_ DOCS/index (Install); CLI: `opencode upgrade --help`

<details><summary><b>PLAT-05</b> Self-update / release channels</summary>

- **candy-code** 🟡 — `candy-code self-update [--check] [--rollback] [--channel=stable|dev]` replaces a release phar after sha256 and minisign checks (signature required when a key is pinned). The default channel follows the running build. `--version` prints the build stamp; releases before `v0.1.1` carry none and must be upgraded by hand. Composer installs update with `composer update`. There is no background update check. — _Evidence:_ `src/Cli/SelfUpdate.php:18,48-54,244-309`; `README.md:120-129`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — `CandyCodeClient.firstVersion` vs the latest `server.hello` version drives `ConnectionBanner`'s "The server was updated" + Reload. Updating is `composer update`. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/src-web/protocol/client.ts:121-124`; `src-web/components/ConnectionBanner.vue`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Checks at startup and periodically, installs in the background, takes effect next launch; `stable` is ~1 week old and skips releases with major regressions. `claude install <version>` pins; `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER`; `claude respawn [--all]` restarts background sessions on the new binary; `/release-notes` version picker (shown in transcript, not sent to Claude); `claude doctor` reports the last update attempt. — _Evidence:_ cc:setup#auto-updates; cc:setup#configure-release-channel; help (`update`, `install`, `respawn`)
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Updates are never installed automatically: the startup check only notifies (`autoupdate: false` disables it; `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE` and `OPENCODE_ALWAYS_NOTIFY_UPDATE` override). `/update` installs a newer 1.x or offers 2.0, and `opencode upgrade [ver] --major` installs v2 and removes v1. Update checks pin to npm `opencode-ai@latest`, and the curl script refuses 2.x. `opencode uninstall` takes `--keep-config` / `--keep-data` / `--dry-run`. — _Evidence:_ v1.19.0 and v1.19.2 release notes; anomalyco/opencode@v1.19.4:packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx (Autoupdate), tui.mdx (`/update`), cli.mdx (`--major`)
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): `autoupdate` true/false/notify on startup; `opencode upgrade [ver] --method`; separate v2 channel (@opencode/cli). v2 (✅): V1 `autoupdate` maps to `update` (`true`→auto, `notify`, `false`→disable). TUI `/update` and post-update highlights dialog (`/highlights`, disable via cli.json `highlights:false`). Both lines are actively released: npm `opencode-ai` latest 1.19.3 and `@opencode/cli` latest 2.0.31 were both published 2026-10-16. — _Evidence:_ V2CLI: `opencode upgrade --help`; V2D/migrate-v1 (autoupdate); V2CL v2.0.28; `npm view opencode-ai`/`@opencode/cli` dist-tags
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Four channels: stable (npm `latest`), extended-stable (a Gateway-only LTS line), beta and dev (git main). Automatic updates, guarded upgrades with Doctor, sealed immutable installation generations with activation and recovery, and a rollback/recovery journal; owners update from chat (`/update`) or Control UI Updates. npm dist-tags: latest 2026.10.7, extended-stable 2026.9.34, beta 2026.10.10-beta.3. — _Evidence:_ `npm view openclaw dist-tags time --json`; `oc@2026.10.7/docs/cli/update.md`; `oc@2026.10.7/docs/install/development-channels.md`

- **candy-code-web** ✅ — Fonts are system stacks, no CDN, no analytics. Only per-viewer conveniences (theme, drafts, tabs, layout) go to localStorage under `candy-code-web:`. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code/src/Server/Http/Responses.php:29-36`; `src-web/stores/storage.ts`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Metrics (latency, reliability, usage) never include code, prompts or file paths; error reports redact secrets/paths/emails; both off by default on Bedrock/Agent Platform/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS. Session-quality surveys separate (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEEDBACK_SURVEY`). Gotcha: turning telemetry off also stops feature-flag fetching, which silently disables flag-dependent features (prompt suggestions, You-should-know mod, Monitor tool, `/skill-doctor`, claude.ai skill sync, Remote Control eligibility). Analytics are sent by the built-in `cc-plugin-telemetry` mod. — _Evidence:_ cc:data-usage#telemetry-services; cc:env-vars#features-that-need-feature-flag-fetching; cc:plugins/mods/overview#mods-built-into-claude-code
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** 🟡 — I grepped OC/, TUI/ and CORE/ for posthog, segment, mixpanel and telemetry SDKs and found none. The web and desktop renderers call `Sentry.init` only when `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` is set at build time, and no user opt-out is documented. Outbound calls: the models catalog (`https://models.opencode.ai`, off with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH`), update checks (`OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`), npm plugin installs, LSP downloads, and share sync only for shared sessions. OpenCode-hosted providers (Zen/Go) receive `x-opencode-*` project/session headers. — _Evidence:_ APP/entry.tsx:133-137; packages/desktop/src/renderer/index.tsx:40-42; CORE/models-dev.ts:160; OC/session/llm/request.ts:184-201
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** 🟡 — I grepped OC/, TUI/ and CORE/ for posthog, segment, mixpanel and telemetry SDKs and found none.
