Outbound calls: the models catalog (`https://models.opencode.ai`, off with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH`), update checks (`OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`), npm plugin installs, LSP downloads, and share sync only for shared sessions. OpenCode-hosted providers (Zen/Go) receive `x-opencode-*` project/session headers. — _Evidence:_ APP/entry.tsx:133-137; packages/desktop/src/renderer/index.tsx:40-42; CORE/models-dev.ts:160; OC/session/llm/request.ts:184-201

<details><summary><b>PLAT-08</b> Offline / air-gapped operation (local models only)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — No provider selected → `EchoProvider` through the full engine (stderr says so on `-p`). A failed LiteLLM refresh keeps the old file and waits a day. Caveat: the package ships `.candy-code/config.dev.json` naming a maintainer demo endpoint (`skynet2.interserver.net`), selectable but never default. — _Evidence:_ `src/Cli/NonInteractive.php:207-221`; `src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:10001-10015`; `candy-code/.candy-code/config.dev.json`; `README.md:156-161`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — Nothing is fetched from outside the server origin; model reachability is the server's concern (sglang/custom local endpoints). — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/dist/index.html`; CSP above
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ❌ — Network access is a system requirement. Air-gapped-ish enterprise setups use Bedrock/Agent Platform/Foundry private endpoints, an LLM gateway, or self-hosted cloud environments, but all still call Claude. Local state (transcripts, checkpoints, memory) is on disk, the agent loop is not. — _Evidence:_ cc:setup#system-requirements; cc:llm-gateway; cc:gateways
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Any local OpenAI-compatible server works through a custom provider using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. This machine runs SGLang on skynet2 that way. Air-gap switches: `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH` / `OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE`, `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD`, `--pure` (no external plugins), and `share: disabled`. Unpinned npm plugins are fetched at startup, so offline use needs pinned or local plugins. websearch/webfetch obviously need network. — _Evidence:_ DOCS/providers (llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama); LOCAL: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc (sglang provider); CLI: `--pure`
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): Local models via Ollama/LM Studio/llama.cpp/any OpenAI-compatible; flags disable models.dev fetch, autoupdate, LSP downloads. v2 (✅): Same capability; custom providers now `providers.<id>.package: "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"` with `settings.baseURL`. Plugins are installed in the background at service start; pinned versions stay offline-safe. — _Evidence:_ V2D/migrate-v1 (Providers); V2D/plugins (Reload)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Local providers ship in core (Ollama local+cloud, SGLang, vLLM, LM Studio); `@openclaw/llama-cpp-provider` installs a verified llama-server + GGUF for chat and local embeddings (`memory.search.provider: "local"`, keyword-only fallback otherwise). `tts-local-cli` plugin, whisper skills, `agent exec --local-model-lean`. Disable update checks for air-gapped. Channels themselves need network. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/gateway/local-models.md`; `oc/docs/concepts/memory-search.md`; `oc/docs/plugins/llama-cpp.md`; `oc/docs/cli/agent.md`

</details>
<details><summary><b>PLAT-09</b> Startup time / footprint</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — Measured on PHP 8.3.6 (no opcache CLI). Help/version/subcommands never construct Program, so they are fast. Footprint dominated by aws-sdk-php and google/cloud-ai-platform. — _Evidence:_ measurements in header of this file; `scratchpad/a3/tools/ttfb.py`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — Measured by the scratch build. The first cold `serve` start here took more than 15 s; warm restarts printed the sign-in line in ~10 s (wall clock incl. PHP start). — _Evidence:_ build output (this audit); `candy-code-web/dist/assets/`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** 🟡 — The 2.1.311 binary is ~280 MiB. Measured locally: `claude --version` ≈10 ms, 36 MB RSS (fast path only, not a full session start). `--bare` skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads and CLAUDE.md discovery (sets CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1); `--safe-mode` disables customizations. Pro/Max relaunches within an hour of the last check skip two network requests, and launches whose only arguments are options start faster. `/heapdump`; `CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT` caps Bash/Monitor memory via cgroup on Linux. — _Evidence:_ local `du -sh ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.311`, `/usr/bin/time claude --version`; help (`--bare`, `--safe-mode`); CL v2.1.311; cc:tools-reference#memory-limit-on-linux-and-wsl
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** 🟡 — Measured 3× on this host on 1.18.35 with `/usr/bin/time opencode --version`: 1.11-1.12 s and 204 MB max RSS for printing the version alone. The 1.19.4 binary is ~215 MB. `opencode debug startup` exists for timing. MCP cold boot is the documented reason for `run --attach` to a warm server. — _Evidence:_ measured locally; CLI: `opencode debug --help`; DOCS/cli (run --attach rationale); `npm view opencode-linux-x64@1.19.4 dist.unpackedSize`
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — `opencode --version` measured 0.15 s / ~89 MB RSS on 2.0.31 (v1: 1.1 s / 200 MB). The 2.1.4 binary is 240 MB unpacked (npm). — _Evidence:_ measured locally on 2.0.31; `npm view @opencode/cli-linux-x64@2.1.4 dist.unpackedSize`
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** 🟡 — Measured on an installed 2026.9.8: `openclaw --version` took 0.14 s wall and 68.7 MB max RSS (Node compile cache warm). The 2026.10.7 npm tarball unpacks to 250 MB across 14,041 files (`dist/` 239 MB). The runtime is a long-lived Gateway process with SQLite state, so startup is not paid per message. No published footprint numbers. — _Evidence:_ Local `/usr/bin/time openclaw --version`; `npm view openclaw@2026.10.7 dist.unpackedSize dist.fileCount`

</details>

<details><summary><b>MOD-18</b> Retries / backoff / rate-limit handling</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `TransientFailure::isTransient` walks the exception chain (Guzzle, openai-php, AWS, Google ApiCore, Anthropic error types). Mid-stream failures resume via continuation/prefill rather than repainting. Connect bound 15 s (`CANDY_CODE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`), stream read-idle 3600 s, turn idle ceiling 120 s (`turnIdleTimeoutSeconds`, re-armed per frame); there is no total-request timeout on any LLM call (Vertex SDK's hidden 60 s deadline is explicitly neutralised). `TransientFailure` honours `Retry-After` (un-jittered, capped), else full-jitter backoff below the ladder ceiling; AWS SDK retries still stack on top. — _Evidence:_ `src/Providers/TransientFailure.php:15-30,140-200,700-703`; `src/Runtime.php:1580-1715`; `src/Providers/Concerns/HttpClientDefaults.php`; `src/Providers/VertexProvider.php:2885-2950`; `src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:75-126`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — Provider retry/backoff is invisible in the web. Transport reconnect: Backoff ±30 %, ladder reset after 60 s up, fresh ticket each try. — _Evidence:_ `src-web/protocol/reconnect.ts:17-74`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Retries 5xx/529/timeouts/dropped connections/429 throttles (not spend-limit 429s, nor requests the API marks not to retry); unparseable tool calls are retried up to twice; gateways that reject a beta value or field are retried without it; `system/api_retry` events in stream-json; `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` waits out 429/529 unattended (`…_MAX_WAIT_MS`, `…_MAX_USAGE_LIMIT_WAIT_MS`, `…_USAGE_LIMIT_RECHECK_MS`); `CLAUDE_CODE_OVERLOADED_RETRY_*` delays. — _Evidence:_ cc:errors#automatic-retries; cc:env-vars; CL v2.1.305; CL v2.1.307; CL v2.1.310; CL v2.1.311
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — RETRY_MAX_RETRIES=5, initial 2000 ms, factor 2, 25% jitter, 30 s cap when there are no headers. Retries on 429/500/502/503/504/524 and overloaded patterns, and honor `retry-after-ms` / `retry-after`. Session status `retry` is shown, including on subagent rows. Defaults: `headerTimeout` and SSE `chunkTimeout` are 5 min. The source applies **no** total `timeout` unless one is set; the docs claim a 300000 default, which the code does not apply. — _Evidence:_ OC/session/retry.ts:26-60; OC/provider/provider.ts:94-125; DOCS/config (timeout)
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): Up to 5 retries, 2 s exponential backoff w/ jitter, honors retry-after(-ms); retry status shown in UI. v2 (✅): Generic retry covers rate limits, provider-internal and unsent/unknown-delivery transport failures and incomplete streams; at most four retries. 2.0.28 raised the streamed-chunk timeout from 5 to 15 min and disabled Bun's fetch idle timeout. 2.0.29 auto-continues responses that hit the output-token limit. Plugins can veto/alter retries via `ctx.session.hook("retry")`. — _Evidence:_ specs/v2/session.md (Retry Is Narrow And Observable); V2CL v2.0.28, v2.0.29; V2D/build/plugins/index (Retry policy)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Recovery continues the transcript after partial output/tool activity instead of resubmitting ("preserve completed work and inspect interrupted actions"); unfinished tool calls are never executed; retry status shown with wait + attempt count. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/concepts/retry.md`; `oc/docs/concepts/model-failover.md`

<details><summary><b>MOD-N3</b> 🆕 Cache warming (keep-alive requests that preserve provider prompt caches while idle)</summary>

- **candy-code** ❌ — No code sends idle requests to keep a provider prefix warm, and a grep for keepalive or cache warm finds only transport/stream keepalives. Vertex and Bedrock cache marks carry no `ttl`, so the provider default of about 5 minutes applies (`BedrockProvider` says it is the only TTL it asks for). CacheHealthWatch deliberately does not count a cache miss after a gap of 240 s or more as a break, because 'providers evict an idle prefix after about five minutes'. The TUI status bar shows the cache hit % and the age of the last report but assumes no TTL. Byte-stable prefixes (PRM-N1) make the cache hit while a session is active; nothing keeps it alive between prompts. — _Evidence:_ `src/Backend/CacheHealthWatch.php:52-59`; `src/Providers/BedrockProvider.php:118-128`; `src/Providers/VertexProvider.php:240`; `src/Renderer.php:2956-2960`
- **candy-code-web** ❌ — As SC. The status bar shows context % and spend only; the `usage.updated` cache fields are not displayed. — _Evidence:_ `src/Backend/CacheHealthWatch.php:52-59`; `candy-code-web/src-web/components/StatusBar.vue`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** 🟡 — Main conversation gets a one-hour TTL by default on Claude subscriptions within plan usage (5 min on API keys/cloud/usage credits); `promptCacheTtl`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL`, `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`, per-subagent `experimental.cacheTtl`; idle compaction (v2.1.299) compacts 200K+ chats ~54 min idle before the 1h cache expires; Pro/Max offer resume-from-summary after long breaks; VS Code shows a cache-expiry clock. Nothing re-sends requests just to keep a cache warm. — _Evidence:_ cc:prompt-caching#cache-lifetime; cc:settings-reference#promptcachettl; CL v2.1.299; cc:vs-code

<details><summary><b>MEM-02</b> Auto-memory (model saves facts without being asked)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `AutoMemoryConsolidator::call` is scheduled from `Chat` when a turn settles and nothing is queued. It reads ≤24 msgs / 24 KB of user and assistant text, redacts secrets, writes in the parent process, and may only touch `auto-memory`-tagged notes. Disabled by `CANDY_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` or `memory.autoConsolidate:false`. — _Evidence:_ `src/Chat.php:2468-2473`; `src/Memory/AutoMemoryConsolidator.php`; `docs/MEMORY.md:506-566`

- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Skips anything derivable from code or already in CLAUDE.md; "remember X" → auto memory, "add to CLAUDE.md" → CLAUDE.md. Changelog references background "memory-extraction" writes. — _Evidence:_ cc:memory#auto-memory; CL v2.1.77 (memory-extraction race fix)

- **OpenCode 2.1.4** 🔌 — opencode-agent-memory's prompt encourages the agent to maintain its blocks. Harness Memory auto-captures evidence from tool interactions. <details><summary><b>MEM-N3</b> 🆕 Standing intents (event-conditioned instructions stored and checked before acting)</summary>

- **candy-code** ❌ — Neither the model nor the user can record "when X happens, do Y" and have it checked before the agent acts. Memory notes are recalled by relevance (the memory-recall block plus the Memory tool's `recall`), not by an event condition. Rule files with `paths:` frontmatter are the only condition-triggered instructions. RulePathNudge delivers a matching rule (or a pointer to it) beside the result of a Read, Grep, Glob, Edit or Write that touches the path. These are user-authored files, the condition can only be a path, and the agent cannot add them as prospective memory. Hooks are event-conditioned, but they are scripts, not instructions to the model. — _Evidence:_ `src/Context/RulePathNudge.php:9-40`; `src/Context/Rule.php` (PathTrigger); `src/Tools/BuiltIn/MemoryTool.php`; no intent tool in `src/Tools/BuiltIn/`

- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ❌ — — — _Evidence:_ OC/
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ❌ — — — _Evidence:_ V2C/

- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Clears older tool outputs, then summarises on the cached prefix (asking once more when the reply holds no summary). Re-injects root CLAUDE.md and unscoped rules, auto memory, the plan, up to 5 recently modified files (>5K tokens come back as `Referenced file`), invoked skill bodies (5K each / 25K total), a rebuilt skill listing (v2.1.304+) and a fresh git snapshot; still-running background work is listed; SessionStart(`compact`) hooks re-run; Ctrl+O shows the tools called before the summary. — _Evidence:_ cc:context-window#what-survives-compaction; CL v2.1.304; CL v2.1.311

A previous summary is passed as `<prior-summary>` with merge rules. The tail is kept verbatim: `preserve_recent_tokens` ?? min(15k, max(2k, 25% of usable)), optional `tail_turns`. The compaction user message is rendered as “What did we do so far?”. The run then appends “Continue if you have next steps…”, which plugins can disable. No file re-reads. — _Evidence:_ CORE/session/compaction.ts:14-55; OC/session/compaction.ts:115-269,531; OC/session/message-v2.ts:241

The summary sits beside the last ~15k tokens kept verbatim (`keep.tokens`), referenced by `metadata.keepID`. `agents.compaction.model` selects another summariser, and overlong compaction requests shorten older tool output first. Provider-native encrypted compaction needs only the same provider and model. — _Evidence:_ compaction.mdx@v2.1.4 L8-23, L91-104, L174; CHANGELOG v2.1.0 (#57091), v2.1.3 (#57564); opencode.ai/changelog v2.1.4 (#58015)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Tool-call/result pairs never split; split-turn prefix summarized separately; read/modified file lists and latest unresolved user request preserved; summary capped (16k chars) with structure-preserving fit; identifierPolicy strict; post-compaction AGENTS.md excerpt; `compaction.model`; pluggable context engines (`plugins.slots.contextEngine`, e.g. Lossless Claw). Safeguard mode audits required headings and identifiers and keeps history when no summary passes. If an automatic compaction's summary times out (summary deadline, HTTP 408 or 504) while the turn is active, the compaction is committed without a summary: recent messages and complete tool pairs stay verbatim and the previous summary carries forward, but older unsummarized facts leave the model context; this is logged with no chat notice. — _Evidence:_ `oc@2026.10.7/docs/concepts/compaction.md` (Auto-compaction; Provider checkpoints); `oc@2026.10.7/docs/concepts/context-engine.md`

<details><summary><b>CTX-N3</b> 🆕 Max-steps wrap-up (on the last allowed step tools are disabled and the agent must summarise)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `EngineBackend::runTurn` loops `for ($step = 0; $step < $this->maxSteps; ...)`. When the loop runs out with tool results still pending (`stepsTruncated`), or the loop guard ended the turn, `summariseStoppedTurn` sends `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED_SUMMARY_PROMPT`: "tools are now disabled. Do not call any tools. Reply to the user with a concise summary of: what has been done, what remains to be done, and the next step". It goes through `StepSummarizer::summaryStep` (no tools). An empty summary leaves the last step's prose in place. Chat then appends the `chat.turn.steps_exhausted` notice: say "continue", or raise `maxToolSteps`. No summary follows a spend-cap stop, because it would be another billed call. Served turns report `stopReason: max_steps`. Task sub-agents default to 200 steps, and delegated runs also get an 80% context wrap-up nudge and a 90% stop. — _Evidence:_ `src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:183-185`, `:405`, `:2485-2514`, `:2784-2800`; `src/Chat.php:2423`, `:19704-19707`; `src/Config/Settings/Definitions/AgentLoopSettings.php:55`; `README.md:2066`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — EngineBackend's summary request runs for served turns. `TranscriptProjector::stopReason` maps `stepsTruncated` to `max_steps`, and the reducer adds a warn notice. A turn the loop guard ended maps to `end_turn`, so it gets no harness notice; only the model's own summary says it was stopped. — _Evidence:_ `src/Host/TranscriptProjector.php:446-455`; `candy-code-web/src-web/stores/reducer.ts:507-513`, `:560-565`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ❌ — Nothing disables tools on the last step to force a summary. — _Evidence:_ cc:sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields; cc:cli-reference
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — When `steps` is reached, an assistant-role MAX_STEPS_PROMPT is appended: tools disabled, respond with what was done, what remains and next steps. — _Evidence:_ OC/session/prompt.ts:1177-1178,1281; CORE/session/runner/max-steps.ts
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): [NEW: Agent max-steps wrap-up] on the last allowed step tools are disabled and a summary-of-progress message is forced. v2 (✅): [NEW: Agent max-steps wrap-up] `steps` still forces a text summary; new user input resets the allowance — _Evidence:_ V2D/agents (Steps); specs/v2/session.md

</details>
<details><summary><b>CTX-N4</b> 🆕 Output-limit auto-continuation (a reply cut off at max output tokens is continued automatically)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — In `EngineBackend::runTurn`, a step whose reply has `lengthStopped`, no tool results and continuable text is sent again, up to `ReplyContinuation::MAX_LENGTH_CONTINUATIONS` = 3 times, while the spend cap and any stop request allow it. Providers that implement AcceptsAssistantPrefill (sglang, vertex, bedrock) get the right-trimmed partial reply as an assistant prefill and continue that same message exactly; if the prefill is rejected, later attempts fall back to the other method. Other providers get the partial reply plus `LENGTH_PROMPT` with the last 64 chars quoted in `<already_delivered_tail>`. Each answer is merged into one reply. If it is still cut after 3 continuations, Chat appends the output-length-stopped notice and served turns report `stopReason: length`. A stream that drops after text was painted is resumed the same way (`RESUME_PROMPT`, Runtime stream retry), so the reply is not painted twice. A length stop on a step that called tools is not continued. — _Evidence:_ `src/Providers/ReplyContinuation.php:7-60`; `src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:1863-1880`, `:1950-1975`; `src/Runtime.php:1543-1569`; `src/Chat.php:2418`, `:19677`; `src/Providers/SglangProvider.php:34`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — The continuation loop runs inside EngineBackend for every served turn, and the joined reply arrives as one `assistant.completed`, so its deltas stream on without a break. After 3 continuations, `TranscriptProjector::stopReason` returns `length`, and the reducer adds the warn notice "Turn stopped: the reply hit the output limit." — _Evidence:_ `src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:1950-1975`; `src/Host/TranscriptProjector.php:450`; `candy-code-web/src-web/stores/reducer.ts:507-513`, `:566`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** 🟡 — Main conversation: "Claude's response exceeded the … output token maximum" error; user replies `continue` (text kept) or raises `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`. Subagents: when a response is cut mid-stream with text but no tool calls, Claude Code prompts them to continue; since 2.1.288 non-interactive sessions and subagents continue from partial responses after mid-response API timeouts; context-limit 400s retried with a smaller `max_tokens`. — _Evidence:_ cc:errors#response-exceeded-the-output-token-maximum; cc:sub-agents#api-errors-in-subagents; CL v2.1.288; cc:errors#automatic-retries
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ❌ — No length-finish continuation in the processor or loop. Added in v2.0.29. — _Evidence:_ OC/session/processor.ts; V2CL v2.0.29
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — Not present in 1.18.35. 2.0.29: preserves partial output and continues with bounded retries, with recovery for truncated tool calls; incomplete streams add a synthetic continuation instruction. — _Evidence:_ V2CL v2.0.29; specs/v2/session.md (Retry)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** 🟡 — When a Responses request hits its output limit while generating a tool call, the admitted tools finish, the partial call is never executed, and the run continues from recorded results (shared retry budget and run deadline). An empty `length` response that leaves no completed or pending reply also continues the transcript with the normal tools, on the same retry budget. A partial text answer stopped at `length` is not continued; it is routed to overflow/error handling. — _Evidence:_ `oc@2026.10.7/docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` (Compaction and retries); `oc@2026.10.7/docs/concepts/retry.md`

</details>

### AGT — Agents & sub-agents

<details><summary><b>AGT-01</b> Primary agent modes (build / plan / ask / ...)</summary>

- **candy-code** 🟡 — The session always runs as one main agent. There is no primary build/plan agent pair, and the main chat cannot run as a preset. The closest thing to a mode is `PermissionMode` (six cases). Plan mode restricts tools to read-only through the gate, and the agent leaves it with the `PlanExit` tool, which puts the plan to the user for approval. <details><summary><b>AGT-N3</b> 🆕 Cross-session messaging between independent top-level sessions (local or remote)</summary>

- **candy-code** 🟡 — SendMessage works hub-and-spoke inside one session: parent to its own sub-agents and back, "never a sibling, a grandchild or another session's run". `/bg`, `/fork` and `Task background:true` run separate daemon sessions. When one settles, its report arrives in the launching session as a user-role message ("[Background session <id> ('<name>') completed]" plus stats), queued behind any running turn. This is one-way and automatic. serve adds `bg.inject`: a client can send a settled background session's answer into any session as a prompt. There is no ListAgents-style discovery, no messaging between two foreground sessions, and nothing across machines. — _Evidence:_ `src/Tools/BuiltIn/SendMessageTool.php:37-45`; `docs/COMMANDS.md:435-442`; `src/Protocol/Methods/BgMethods.php:36-57`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — In serve, background results do not land in chat by themselves; `bg.inject` closes that gap manually and admits the report like a typed prompt (queued by default). Agents cannot message other sessions (SendMessage is intra-session). — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/src-web/components/panels/BackgroundPanel.vue:72`; `candy-code-web/src-web/stores/agents/background.ts:89-91`; `src/Protocol/Methods/BgMethods.php:36-57`

### SKL — Skills

<details><summary><b>SKL-01</b> SKILL.md format support (frontmatter name/description)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — A frontmatter block is required. Fields are typed through `SkillFrontmatter`, and a mistyped field skips that skill only. Bodies are scrubbed to valid UTF-8. Each file is capped at 1 MiB and its frontmatter at 64 KiB. Unknown or inert keys are named in one launch row. — _Evidence:_ `src/Skills/SkillFrontmatter.php`; `src/Skills/SkillFileReader.php:44,52`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — SKILL.md parsing is the engine's. The web's Context panel (`context.sources`) lists every registered skill by name, `SkillOrigin` tier and `disabledSkills` state; descriptions and format badges are not sent. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code/src/Host/ContextSources.php:153-157`; `candy-code-web/src-web/components/panels/ContextPanel.vue:132-142`; `candy-code-web/src-web/components/panels/SidePanels.vue:102`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Fields: name, description, when_to_use, argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context, agent, background, hooks, paths, shell, metadata, license, compatibility. Unknown fields silently ignored; unparsable YAML loads with no fields. Uploads to claude.ai/Skills API accept only the six spec fields. — _Evidence:_ cc:skills#frontmatter-reference; cc:skills#using-skill-frontmatter-outside-claude-code
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Docs: name 1-64 chars matching `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` and equal to the directory name; description 1-1024 chars. The loader only requires `name` to be a string. Skills without a description load but are not advertised. Duplicate names are reported. — _Evidence:_ DOCS/skills; OC/skill/index.ts:50-56,120-140,321-323
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): SKILL.md with name (dir-matching, kebab) + description; license/compatibility/metadata accepted, others ignored. v2 (✅): Accepts license/compatibility but ignores them; `disable-model-invocation`/`metadata.opencode/autoinvoke:false` hide from the model. — _Evidence:_ V2D/skills (Discovery, Frontmatter, IDs)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — YAML parsed first with single-line fallback; nested metadata re-parsed as JSON5; `{baseDir}` placeholder; legacy `metadata.clawdbot` honored. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/skills.md` (SKILL.md format)

</details>
<details><summary><b>SKL-02</b> Discovery locations (user / project / plugin / bundled)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — SkillManager::loadAll()` walks tiers built-in < project < user; inside a tier, bundle trees register first, then `.agents`, `.claude`, `.opencode`, then native, so the last write wins and every displaced skill is recorded for the launch notice. Bundles come from `~/.candy-code/bundles`, `<root>/.candy-code/bundles` and the user-tier `pluginPaths` list. Symlinks are followed but confined; the walk stops at depth 7 or 2000 directories. — _Evidence:_ `src/Skills/SkillManager.php:113-170`; `src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:2273-2290,4952-4955`; `src/Skills/SkillLoader.php:189,205

### MCP — Model Context Protocol

<details><summary><b>MCP-01</b> Client: stdio</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — Servers start once at launch and are shared across forked turns behind a cross-process lock. A shutdown hook stops them. — _Evidence:_ `src/MCP/McpClient.php:161,524`; `src/MCP/StdioMcpServer.php`; `src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:8408,8794`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — Served sessions inherit the launch's stdio client. The web Context panel (`context.sources`) lists each declared project server with its transport and a `trusted` badge read from the config census, not from liveness, and drops the user-tier rows the census computes. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/src-web/components/panels/ContextPanel.vue:144-158`; `candy-code/src/Host/ContextSources.php:147-173`; `candy-code/src/Cli/McpDecision.php:295-340`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Process-tree shutdown; `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup; 30-min idle tool timeout default for stdio. — _Evidence:_ help (`mcp add`); cc:mcp#option-3-add-a-local-stdio-server
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Options: command, environment, cwd, enabled, timeout (tool fetch, default 5 s per docs; 30 s connect default in code). — _Evidence:_ DOCS/mcp-servers (Local); OC/mcp/index.ts:38,345-360
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — Options: command, environment, cwd, enabled, timeout (tool fetch, default 5 s per docs; 30 s connect default in code). — _Evidence:_ DOCS/mcp-servers (Local); OC/mcp/index.ts:38,345-360
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — stdio servers (command/args/env/cwd) with owned process-group cleanup — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/mcp.md`; `oc/docs/plugins/bundles.md` (Transports)

</details>
<details><summary><b>MCP-02</b> Client: SSE</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — SseMcpServer` speaks the 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport: one GET event stream on a raw deadline-bounded socket, POSTs via Guzzle; the server's `endpoint` event must share the configured URL's origin or is refused before any POST; a dropped stream fails the in-flight call and retries a bounded backoff burst; `type: "sse"` entries (Claude dialect) route here. — _Evidence:_ `src/MCP/SseMcpServer.php:13-60`; `src/MCP/McpClient.php:760-775
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — Same census row as MCP-01: name + transport + trust badge; no stream state. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/src-web/components/panels/ContextPanel.vue:150-155`; `candy-code/src/Host/ContextSources.php:162-171`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Docs keep it as an option alongside HTTP. — _Evidence:_ cc:mcp#option-2-add-a-remote-sse-server
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — The transports list is [StreamableHTTP, SSE], tried in order. — _Evidence:_ OC/mcp/index.ts:268-300
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ❌ — v1 (✅): Remote servers fall back to SSE transport if Streamable HTTP fails. v2 (❌): SSE transport removed: remote servers use Streamable HTTP only — _Evidence:_ V2C/mcp/client.ts:10,272-277; V2D/mcp-servers (Remote)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — SSE (the default when a URL server omits `transport`) — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/plugins/bundles.md` (Transports)

</details>
<details><summary><b>MCP-03</b> Client: Streamable HTTP</summary>

- **candy-code** 🟡 — HttpMcpServer` POSTs every message with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, reads the reply buffered (not `stream => true`, measured hostile), re-initialises when a session-bearing request gets 404, sends a session DELETE on stop, never follows redirects, and advertises protocol 2024-11-05. No standalone GET listener exists, so server-pushed notifications/requests outside a reply are never received. — _Evidence:_ `src/MCP/HttpMcpServer.php:14-17,42,84,92,304-322,558-575,700-735
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — As MCP-02. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/src-web/components/panels/ContextPanel.vue:150-155`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Two client runtimes (MCP TS SDK 1.x / 2.0 with protocol 2026-07-28); 16 MiB response cap; discovery cache opt-in; a call pending when an HTTP connection drops is repeated once only for tools marked `readOnlyHint`/`idempotentHint`. — _Evidence:_ cc:mcp#mcp-client-runtimes; cc:mcp#mark-tools-that-are-safe-to-call-twice; CL v2.1.307
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Headers go via requestInit. — _Evidence:_ OC/mcp/index.ts:268-283; DOCS/mcp-servers (Remote)
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): type remote: Streamable HTTP tried first, custom headers. v2 (✅): Streamable HTTP; optional MCP 2026-07-28 protocol via `protocol: auto/2026-07-28` — _Evidence:_ V2D/mcp-servers (Protocol version)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — `transport: "streamable-http"` with headers (${ENV}), TLS/mTLS, timeouts — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/mcp.md`

</details>
<details><summary><b>MCP-04</b> OAuth for remote MCP servers</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — candy-code mcp auth login <server>` runs PKCE against a 127.0.0.1 loopback listener (300 s human-wait bound), supports scopes, stores tokens in `~/.local/share/candy-code/mcp-auth.json` and refreshes ahead of expiry; no RFC 8707 `resource` parameter. In the TUI `/mcp login <server>` forks that CLI arm (`McpLoginFork`) and announces the URL; `/mcp reconnect` restarts servers behind a config-drift gate. Tokens attach at the next launch. — _Evidence:_ `src/MCP/OAuthLoopbackFlow.php:51,215-239`; `src/Chat.php:19810-19843`; `src/Support/McpLoginFork.php:12-28`; `src/MCP/HttpMcpServer.php:962-975`; `src/MCP/OAuthClientRegistration.php:365-386,904-913`; `lang/en.php:1257
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — A served `/mcp` runs `McpAuthHostCommand` → `McpAuthCommand::execute()`, whose `login` arm prints the `candy-code mcp auth login …` guidance; only `Chat::handleMcpAuthCommand` intercepts `login <server>` to fork the flow, and the listener binds 127.0.0.1 on the server host, so a remote browser cannot finish it. Tokens stored by a host-side CLI login do ride served http servers. — _Evidence:_ `src/Host/Commands/McpAuthHostCommand.php:19-26`; `src/Commands/McpAuthCommand.php:167-173,308-313`; `src/Chat.php:19810-19820`; `lang/en.php:1264`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Re-auth prompt when a server asks for more scope (v2.1.288); tokens per endpoint; claude.ai connectors pre-authenticated. — _Evidence:_ cc:mcp#authenticate-with-remote-mcp-servers; help (`mcp login`); CL v2.1.288
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Status `needs_client_registration` / `needs_auth`. `oauth:false` disables it. `opencode mcp debug <name>` tests connectivity and discovery. — _Evidence:_ DOCS/mcp-servers (OAuth); OC/mcp/oauth-provider.ts; CLI: `opencode mcp --help`
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): Auto OAuth on 401 with DCR (RFC 7591) or pre-registered client; `mcp auth/logout/debug`; tokens in mcp-auth.json. v2 (✅): OAuth with PKCE via pre-registered client, CIMD, or DCR; snake_case oauth fields; /mcps sign-in — _Evidence:_ V2D/mcp-servers (OAuth)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Per-requester identity servers supported. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/mcp.md` (An HTTP server needs authorization)

</details>

### TL — Built-in tools

<details><summary><b>TL-01</b> Read file</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — Returns `N: text` lines with a next-offset footer; a long file read without offset/limit gets an LSP or regex outline (≤200 rows / 8 KiB). Binary files answer with a note instead of mojibake: in-cap images ride the result (TL-19), PDFs get a `pdftotext` hint (TL-20). Line counting stops at an 8 MiB scan budget (footer then says `of ≥N`); jailed via `PathJail::resolve`, records stat + hash into the shared ReadLedger. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/Read.php:46,54,62,93,101-102,423-427,726-763`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — — — _Evidence:_ `src-web/components/ToolCard.vue`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Absolute paths; empty-file and past-EOF notices; refuses directories; `cat`/`head`/`sed -n`/`rg` on one file also count as reads. — _Evidence:_ cc:tools-reference#read-tool-behavior
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Rejects binary. `*.env` asks by default. Triggers nested AGENTS.md. — _Evidence:_ OC/tool/read.ts; OC/tool/read.txt
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): read: files, directories (listing), images, PDFs; offset/limit paging. v2 (✅): read: files, non-recursive dir listings, images/PDF ≤20 MiB; listings also trigger nested AGENTS.md — _Evidence:_ V2D/tools (Read); V2C/tool/plugin/read.ts
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Pages fit the model's tool-result budget; BOM/Windows decoding; credential redaction; "did you mean" sibling filename hints. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/code-mode/guest-api.md`; `oc/dist/tools-BEx53dKD.mjs` (read tool)

</details>
<details><summary><b>TL-02</b> Write file</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `resolveForCreate` anchors containment at the nearest existing ancestor, normalises `..` lexically first and refuses dangling symlinks. An existing file needs `overwrite: true`. `AtomicFileWriter::replace` writes temp+fsync+rename, keeps mode/uid/gid and writes hard-linked files in place. ReadLedger stale check runs if the file was read before. The result carries a unified diff of the overwrite (diff bound applies). — _Evidence:_ `src/Tools/BuiltIn/Write.php:49,146,197-208,233-279,286,299`; `src/Tools/PathJail.php:181-254`; `src/Support/AtomicFileWriter.php:184-220`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — — — _Evidence:_ `src-web/components/DiffView.vue`; `e2e/session.spec.ts:27`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Refuses writing through symlinks; won't write back U+FFFD garbled text. — _Evidence:_ cc:tools-reference#write-tool-behavior
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Gated by the `edit` permission; the diff is shown in the ask dialog. — _Evidence:_ OC/tool/write.ts:18,74-90; DOCS/tools (write)
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): write: create/overwrite; formatter + LSP errors for the file and up to 5 others. v2 (✅): write creates/replaces files, may format; no LSP diagnostics — _Evidence:_ V2D/tools (Write); V2C/tool/plugin/write.ts:44
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Memory-flush turns get an append-only write; `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` optional containment. — _Evidence:_ `oc/dist/tools-BEx53dKD.mjs` (file-write-verification); `oc/docs/gateway/permission-modes.md`

</details>
<details><summary><b>TL-03</b> Edit (exact string replace)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `old_string` must be unique. `replace_all` applies to exact matches only, and a loose match never applies to more than one place. On failure the error names the matching lines or the closest lines. Output: `File updated: path (+a -r lines)` plus a diff payload for the TUI. <details><summary><b>TL-09</b> Bash / shell</summary>

<details><summary><b>TL-10</b> Background shell + output polling / monitor</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — run_in_background: true` starts the (cd-guarded, sandbox-wrapped) command through the containment spawn, records pid = pgid, streams stdio to owner-only files and answers a `sh-xxxxxxxx` id at once; ShellOutput reads from a byte cursor, ShellStop sends TERM→grace→KILL to the group. Shells are killed at 1800 s and at teardown; output is capped at 64 MiB. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/Bash.php:422,577-588`; `candy-code/src/Background/BackgroundShellRegistry.php:142,164,982`; `candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/ShellOutput.php:83-92`; `candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/ShellStop.php:20-22,82
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — Served sessions get Bash `run_in_background` plus ShellOutput/ShellStop because `tools()` threads the launch's BackgroundShellRegistry into the catalog build; their calls render as ordinary cards, and foreground Bash streams a live tail. The registry is one table per server process and workspace root (`forSession('main')`), so concurrent served sessions in one root share it. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code/src/Cli/LaunchContext.php:690-694,1708`; `candy-code/src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:8396-8406`; `candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/ShellOutput.php:50,66`; `candy-code/src/Tools/BuiltIn/ShellStop.php:56,72`

<details><summary><b>TL-N2</b> 🆕 Tool-loop / doom-loop detection (identical repeated tool calls detected and interrupted)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — ToolCallLoopGuard keeps one ledger per turn, keyed by tool name + canonicalised arguments (map keys sorted recursively) + an xxh128 hash of the result. A poll whose output changes therefore never counts, and counting is per signature across the turn, so an A/B ping-pong is caught. It runs on the hook chain. RepeatCallCountHook (PostToolUse) appends "[Repeat-call loop guard: identical call #n …]" to the result from the 3rd call. RepeatCallGuardHook (PreToolUse) refuses from the 5th, and refused attempts keep counting. EngineBackend ends the turn at the 8th and asks for a no-tools summary that must say the turn was stopped; the TUI also adds the `chat.turn.loop_guard` notice. It is registered every turn, even when hooks are disabled, and sub-agents get it too. Limits: five identical calls in ONE message are all admitted (batch gating), and the thresholds cannot be configured. — _Evidence:_ `src/Backend/ToolCallLoopGuard.php:7-61`, `:93-160`; `src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:1525`, `:2495-2506`, `:5382-5383`; `src/Chat.php:2427-2429`, `:19721-19727`; `README.md:2066`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — The hooks are registered per turn inside EngineBackend, the path every served turn takes. The appended warning text and the refusal reason render in the cards. — _Evidence:_ `src/Backend/EngineBackend.php:5382-5383`; `src/Host/TranscriptProjector.php:446-455`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ❌ — Workflow schema retries stop after 5; auto mode pauses after 3 consecutive / 20 total classifier blocks. — _Evidence:_ cc:how-claude-code-works#when-context-fills-up; cc:hooks#stop-decision-control; cc:permission-modes#when-auto-mode-falls-back
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — DOOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD=3. Defaults to ask. This host sets `doom_loop: allow` everywhere. — _Evidence:_ OC/session/processor.ts:29,356-373; DOCS/permissions (Available Permissions)
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ❌ — v1 (✅): [NEW: Doom-loop guard] same tool call repeated 3× with identical input triggers a `doom_loop` permission ask. v2 (❌): [NEW: Doom-loop guard] removed — `doom_loop` is not a v2 permission action — _Evidence:_ V2D/permissions (Actions note)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** 🟡 — Three consecutive identical tool errors (same tool, arguments and error result) always end the turn with a recorded error and recovery guidance, even with `tools.loopDetection.enabled: false`; changed arguments or results, and successful calls, reset the streak. ### EDT — Editing & code intelligence

<details><summary><b>EDT-01</b> Edit fuzzy / whitespace-tolerant matching</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — Disproportionately large or small loose matches are refused. new_string is re-indented to the shift, CRLF is kept by the fuzzy stages, and the result names the stage that matched. Failure hints list the closest lines. ApplyPatch uses the same chain. — _Evidence:_ `src/Tools/Edit/EditMatcher.php:43-213`; `src/Tools/Edit/IndentShift.php:50-53`; `src/Tools/Edit/*Matcher.php`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — Hook- and matcher-annotated result text rides `tool.finished` and the card prints it under the diff. — _Evidence:_ `src/Tools/BuiltIn/Edit.php:108`; `candy-code-web/src-web/components/ToolCard.vue:39,81-82`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ❌ — One whitespace difference misses; Claude retries with more context. — _Evidence:_ cc:tools-reference#edit-tool-behavior
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Block-anchor: ≥3 lines, trimmed first and last lines as anchors, similarity threshold 0.65. A candidate must be unique unless replaceAll. Refuses if the matched span is ≥2× the lines or >4× the chars of oldString. — _Evidence:_ OC/tool/edit.ts:217-701
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** 🟡 — v1 (✅): Replacers: exact, line-trimmed, block-anchor (Levenshtein), whitespace, indentation, escape, boundary, context, multi. v2 (🟡): Only typographic-variant and trailing-whitespace fallbacks (v1 had a 9-stage replacer chain) — _Evidence:_ V2C/tool/plugin/edit.ts:223
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — Mismatch errors list up to 3 closest lines with similarity and indentation/escaping hints. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/index.md`; prior report `11-openclaw.md` §6.1 (re-checked against `oc/dist/tools-BEx53dKD.mjs`)

</details>

### PER — Permissions & safety

<details><summary><b>PER-01</b> Permission modes (default / acceptEdits / plan / bypass / auto)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — The order is breaker, then rules (first match), then the mode's evaluator. Read-only shell lines run unasked in default and accept-edits. accept-edits grants in-root Edit/Write/ApplyPatch and scoped mkdir/touch/rmdir. — _Evidence:_ `src/Permissions/PermissionMode.php:11-193`; `src/Permissions/PermissionGate.php:587-1108`; `src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:178-180`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — — — _Evidence:_ `src-web/components/StatusBar.vue:6`; `candy-code/docs/SERVER.md:602-605`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — Auto = classifier reviews actions (server-side review on 1P); deny rules apply in every mode; auto needs supported models (Opus/Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable). Interactive terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto (v2.1.283+); `claude -p` and Agent SDK runs with no mode set start in Manual and deny calls needing approval unless a rule, hook, `canUseTool` or `--permission-prompt-tool` approves (v2.1.302+). The CLI flag spells Manual as `manual`, settings and SDK as `default`. — _Evidence:_ cc:permission-modes#which-mode-a-session-starts-in; cc:permission-modes#tool-calls-denied-in-claude--p-and-agent-sdk-runs; help (`--permission-mode` choices); CL v2.1.302

- **OpenCode 2.1.4** 🟡 — v1 (🟡): allow/ask/deny rules + `--auto` (approve all not denied); plan agent; no named acceptEdits-style modes. Default: allow. v2 (🟡): Ordered allow/ask/deny `permissions` array + `--auto`; per-project auto-accept (desktop mod+shift+a) — _Evidence:_ V2D/permissions; V2CL v2.0.28

<details><summary><b>PER-03</b> Allow / deny / ask rules with patterns (e.g. Bash(git:*))</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — An allow rule must cover every segment and fails closed on substitution or a writing redirect. A deny/ask rule fires on any segment and also binds Bash and PtyRun to each other. Patterns written with operators are matched by structure. Verified-by-repro: deny `Bash(rm:*)` lets `rm -rf build` through (allow `Bash(git:*)` grants nothing). — _Evidence:_ `src/Permissions/PermissionRule.php:195-207,385-468,691-942,1012-1105`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — `permission.rules` (Scope::Read) answers mode, modeSource, rules and sessionGrants. The Rules side panel renders them read-only and reloads on session switch, using a generation latch against the switch race. Rules change only in settings files, and the mode moves through the status-bar select. — _Evidence:_ `web:components/panels/RulesPanel.vue:7-55`; `src/Protocol/Methods/PermissionMethods.php:53,213-227`; `web:components/panels/SidePanels.vue:98`

### UI — TUI / GUI UX

<details><summary><b>UI-01</b> Full-screen TUI vs inline rendering</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `bin/candy-code` boots `App`, a pane shell that hosts the `Chat` model as one component tree. It enters the alternate screen (`\e[?1049h`), so the transcript is in-app scrollback, not terminal scrollback. Frame = menu bar row (menus + pane tabs + "Currently: X"), optional session-tab strip, left/right docked pane columns, a bordered chat pane and a one-row status bar. Frame is clipped to `rows` and every line is fitted to `cols` (no overflow seen at 140, 80 or 50 columns). There is no inline/no-alt-screen mode like Claude Code's default. — _Evidence:_ `src/App/App.php`; `src/Tui/Renderer.php:133-210`; `src/Renderer.php:1918-1966`; `src/Chat.php:10603-10608` (alt screen); README.md:186-190
- **candy-code-web** ➖ — — — _Evidence:_ `src-web/App.vue`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — `/tui fullscreen/default` relaunches with the conversation intact; fullscreen keeps memory flat, adds mouse, fixed input box, in-app search; screen-reader mode forces classic. — _Evidence:_ cc:fullscreen#fullscreen-by-default; cc:commands (/tui)
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ✅ — Mini mode keeps scrollback immutable, with a repaintable footer for prompt, permission and question. It supports `--no-replay` / `--replay-limit`. — _Evidence:_ OC/cli/cmd/tui.ts:123-175; OC/cli/cmd/run/footer.ts:1-26
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ✅ — v1 (✅): Full-screen OpenTUI app by default; `--mini` / `run -i` inline split-footer mode writing to native scrollback. v2 (✅): Full-screen TUI by default; `opencode mini` inline interface — _Evidence:_ V2D/cli/index (Mini); V2CLI: `opencode mini --help`
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ✅ — `TuiMainScreen`: "renders into the terminal's main screen and scrollback" (alt-screen variant exists in pi-tui but OpenClaw's TUI uses main screen). Plus native desktop/mobile apps. — _Evidence:_ `oc/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/tui-main-screen.d.ts`; `oc/dist/tui-sA-O8ceh.mjs`; `oc/docs/web/tui.md`

</details>
<details><summary><b>UI-02</b> Themes (count) & custom themes</summary>

- **candy-code** 🟡 — `/theme`, palette "Switch theme" or the settings view. Persisted to `config.json`. The `adaptive` theme follows the terminal background (OSC 11 reply, `COLORFGBG`, `CANDY_CODE_BACKGROUND`). Every chrome colour is projected along HSL lightness until it clears WCAG contrast against the detected background *and* the row-highlight fill, so even `light` stays readable on a dark terminal. No user theme files or overrides: `Theme::byName` throws for any name not in the fixed list. The picker opens on the current theme (● marker), and the palette and menu labels match. — _Evidence:_ `src/Theme.php:60,139-180,237-330`; `src/Tui/TerminalBackground.php`; live: `/theme`, palette

The TUI's dracula/tokyoNight/ansi sets are not mirrored. — _Evidence:_ `web:stores/settings.ts:5,23-40`; `web:styles/tokens.css`

<details><summary><b>UI-07</b> Vim mode</summary>

<details><summary><b>UI-N5</b> 🆕 Prompt hygiene (strip invisible Unicode before sending; spellcheck)</summary>

- **candy-code** 🟡 — sugar-core's InputReader sanitises bracketed paste (`ProgramOptions::$sanitizePaste`, default true, which applies `Sanitize::untrusted`). That removes every ESC/CSI/OSC/DCS sequence, C0 controls except TAB/LF/CR, DEL and C1. The Renderer draws the in-progress input and user rows through `untrustedForDisplay` → `markInvisibleFormatting`, so these become visible `<U+XXXX>` markers: U+200B, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+2060 and U+FEFF always, and ZWJ/ZWNJ/LRM/RLM/ALM unless they follow a non-ASCII character. That makes Trojan-Source text visible. `untrusted` keeps these characters for paste fidelity, so they reach the model unchanged (CC strips them). There is no spellcheck. — _Evidence:_ `sugar-core/src/ProgramOptions.php:160`; `sugar-core/src/Util/Sanitize.php:239-262`, `:320-380`; `src/Renderer.php:84-89`, `:1628`; `src/Chat.php:2798-2800`
- **candy-code-web** 🟡 — The composer `<textarea>` sets no `spellcheck` attribute, so the browser default applies (on for textareas in Chrome and Firefox). `session.send` passes the text through unchanged. — _Evidence:_ `candy-code-web/src-web/components/Composer.vue:109-119`; `src/Protocol/Methods/TurnMethods.php:56-67`
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — — — _Evidence:_ cc:interactive-mode#invisible-characters-in-prompts; cc:interactive-mode#check-spelling-as-you-type
- **OpenCode 1.19.4** ❌ — — — _Evidence:_ TUI/component/prompt/ (grep)
- **OpenCode 2.1.4** ❌ — — — _Evidence:_ V2T/component/prompt/ (grep)
- **OpenClaw 2026.10.7** ❌ — Related hygiene elsewhere: progress-card text drops invisible/bidi characters, macOS approval panels show visible escapes for invisible characters, Control UI strips leaked control tokens from assistant output. — _Evidence:_ `oc/docs/tools/progress-card.md`; `oc/docs/tools/exec-approvals.md`; `oc/docs/web/control-ui/chat.md`

</details>

<details><summary><b>WEB-11</b> Web UI auth & security model</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — Host allow-list. Origin check on every upgrade and non-GET. Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site refused. Headers: CSP, nosniff, DENY, no-referrer, COOP, CORP. Port-scoped cookie name. Logout ends the cookie session and closes its sockets. The sign-in lockout never falls on the owner token. Token rotation signs everyone out (4001). Cookie sessions persist hash-only across restarts (0600, pruned on boot). — _Evidence:_ `src/Server/Http/AuthMiddleware.php:211-227`; `src/Server/Http/ApiController.php:31,133-153`; `src/Server/Auth/RateLimiter.php:14-27`; `src/Server/Auth/CookieSessions.php:16-19`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — The page never holds the token: a code in the URL fragment becomes an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict, port-scoped cookie, then a 30 s single-use ticket per socket. Login lockout never blocks a valid token, and logging out closes the session's sockets. — _Evidence:_ `web:protocol/auth.ts`

<details><summary><b>WEB-N3</b> 🆕 Lossless reconnect (resume the event stream from a cursor without gaps or duplicates)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — The server logs durable events with a gap-free per-session `seq` before broadcast. 20,000 are kept in the session DB, so seqs continue across restarts. The attach client redials after 0.25 s, doubling to 4 s, for up to 12 attempts, and re-says `server.hello` with `resume: {sessionId: lastSeq}`. When the log can no longer serve the cursor, it stitches a paged reset snapshot. A deliberate close, a refused resume or an exhausted ladder ends the redial. — _Evidence:_ `src/Host/RemoteSessionHost.php:85-95,866-935`; `docs/SERVER.md:990-1000`
- **candy-code-web** ✅ — Watchdog closes a socket silent for 2× tick (30 s). Verified by e2e "a dropped socket reconnects and resumes". — _Evidence:_ `src-web/protocol/client.ts:149-174,321-339`; `e2e/reconnect.spec.ts:5`

### AUT — Automation / headless

<details><summary><b>AUT-01</b> Non-interactive mode (-p / run)</summary>

- **candy-code** ✅ — `NonInteractive::run` builds the engine backend, closes AskUser/PlanExit and prints the final message. `-p` defaults to bypass-permissions, with a stderr notice. `--max-turns` overrides the step ceiling (default 1000). `maxCostUsd`/`CANDY_CODE_MAX_COST` are validated and enforced. Hooks fire on `-p` runs. Each run is saved to a session row, the json envelope carries `session_id` and usage, and `--resume` works. — _Evidence:_ `src/Cli/NonInteractive.php:275,295-311,643-651`; `src/Cli/Bootstrap.php:189-197`
- **candy-code-web** ➖ — —
- **Claude Code 2.1.311** ✅ — `--bare` for reproducible CI. With no `--permission-mode` (or `permissions.defaultMode`) a print run starts in Manual and denies calls needing approval unless an allow rule, hook or `--permission-prompt-tool` approves them (v2.1.302+); `--permission-prompts none` denies anything that would prompt. — _Evidence:_ help (`-p`, `--permission-prompts`); cc:headless; cc:permission-modes#tool-calls-denied-in-claude--p-and-agent-sdk-runs

Desktop scheduled tasks run locally; session crons expire after 7 days. — _Evidence:_ cc:routines; cc:desktop-scheduled-tasks; cc:scheduled-tasks; CL v2.1.311

- **candy-code** ✅ — `/loop <interval> <prompt>` (seconds, or an s/m/h/d suffix) registers an ephemeral row whose prompt queues as the next turn each interval. The first fire comes one interval out. Rows end with the process or with `/schedules delete`. TUI only; see AUT-08 web. — _Evidence:_ `src/Host/Commands/LoopCommand.php:5-81`; `src/Chat.php:18556-18566`

Only Chat's pump fires ephemeral rows; `ScheduleRegistry::fireDue()`, the serve path, skips them. A browser-typed loop therefore silently never runs. — _Evidence:_ `src/Host/Commands/LoopCommand.php:63-81`; `src/Background/ScheduleRegistry.php:391-397`; `src/Chat.php:18556-18566`; `src/Host/SessionHost.php:1647`

## Appendix B — Method and sources

**Process.**
1. **Shared taxonomy.** Nine research agents filled the same 356-row taxonomy across 25 categories. Six audited candy-code and candy-code-web: context/memory, extensibility, engine/sessions/CLI, tools/safety, TUI, and web/server. Three researched Claude Code, OpenCode and OpenClaw.
2. **Extra rows.** Features found outside the taxonomy became 🆕 rows (53 in all). The original 42 were rated for every product; the 11 added on 2026-10-26 carry `· Not assessed` where a product's research did not cover them. A separate pass compared the OpenCode 1.x and 2.x lines, at 1.19.4 and 2.1.4.
3. **Verification.** Every issue an audit reported was re-checked by a separate adversarial verifier (6 passes). Verifiers confirmed, corrected, downgraded or rejected each claim.
4. **Merge.** Rows were merged mechanically by row ID, so every cell in §3 is the rating of the agent that studied that product. Narrative sections §1, §4, §5 and §6 were written from the agents' deep-dive reports.
5. **Refresh (2026-10-26).** Three static audits re-checked every candy-code and candy-code-web cell and its Appendix A bullet against monorepo `master`, and three competitor passes moved the columns to Claude Code 2.1.311, OpenCode 1.19.4 / 2.1.4 and OpenClaw 2026.10.7. The reports are in `prompt_kit/findings/comparison-1026/`: `cc-audit-k1.md`, `cc-audit-k2.md`, `cc-audit-k3.md`, `comp-claude-code.md`, `comp-opencode.md` and `comp-openclaw.md`. The §2 scoreboard is recomputed from the §3 glyphs by `prompt_kit/findings/comparison-1026/apply_comparison.py --check`.

**candy-code and candy-code-web.**
- Source under `candy-code/src/`, `candy-code/docs/`, `candy-code/README.md`, `candy-code-web/src-web/`, `candy-code/src/Server/`, `candy-code/src/Protocol/`. Reachability was traced from `bin/candy-code`.
- Live runs:
  - the TUI in tmux (isolated HOME, scratch project, dev SGLang endpoint);
  - headless `-p`;
  - throwaway `candy-code serve` instances probed with curl, WebSocket and headless Chromium;
  - `npm run typecheck`, `lint` and `test`;
  - a byte-for-byte rebuild of `dist/`.
- The 2026-10-26 refresh read `candy-code/src`, `candy-code/builtin-commands` and `candy-code-web/src-web` statically (monorepo sources, not vendor copies) and ran no tests.
- The repo was never modified.

**Claude Code 2.1.311.**
- Official docs at <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/>: all 228 pages listed in `llms.txt`, fetched on 2026-10-26 and searched.
- Changelog: <https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md> (through 2.1.311).
- `claude --help` and every subcommand's `--help`.
- A read-only look at `~/.claude` (plugin marketplace catalogs list 315 entries).
- Direct observation of what a Claude Code session/subagent is handed (system reminders, deferred tools, memory blocks).

**OpenCode 1.19.4 and 2.1.4.**
- Source at the 1.18.35, 1.19.4, 2.0.31 and 2.1.4 tags of <https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode> (`packages/opencode/src/`, v2 `packages/core`), the docs shipped with each tag, the v2 `CHANGELOG.md`, <https://opencode.ai/changelog> and <https://opencode.ai/docs/>. v1 notes are GitHub releases; v2 tags have none.
- `opencode --help` and subcommand help; `npm view opencode-ai` and `npm view @opencode/cli` (1.19.4 published 2026-10-22, 2.1.4 on 2026-10-23).
- The installed copy is 1.18.35; every 1.18.35 → 1.19.4 behaviour difference was read from source. v2.1.4's notes exist only on opencode.ai/changelog.
- Read-only local configs: `~/.config/opencode/` and the repo's `.opencode/`.
- npm metadata, READMEs and tarballs of ecosystem plugins (opencode-goal-plugin, opencode-pty, magic-context, DCP, opencode-agent-memory, supermemory, plannotator, oh-my-openagent, …).

**OpenClaw 2026.10.7.**
- The installed 2026.9.8 package as the baseline (`openclaw/docs/` ≈1,300 pages, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `skills/`, `dist/`) and the `clawhub` CLI.
- `openclaw --help` and subcommand help.
- <https://docs.openclaw.ai>, the 2026.10.7 npm package (docs + `dist/`, diffed against the installed 2026.9.8), and the per-version changelogs 2026.9.9–2026.10.7 (`CHANGELOG/<ver>.md` on GitHub). 2026.10.5 is the feature release and 10.1 carries a smaller change set; the other releases are mostly models, reliability and security fixes. npm `latest` is 2026.10.7 (published 2026-10-24).

**Prior internal research.** Used as leads only and re-verified: `prompt_kit/findings/crush-report/*` (2026-10-01/02) and `docs/old/crush_report.md` / `crush_feat.md`. <!-- @rename-keep historical provenance -->

**Raw material.** The 2026-10-26 reports, with every changed cell's detail and evidence, are under `prompt_kit/findings/comparison-1026/`. The original compile's per-agent working papers are not part of the repo; their detail and evidence text is reproduced in Appendix A.
